title: cljplot2
text:
cljplot2
cljplot2 is a Clojure plotting library rendering static images with clojure2d. A plot is a plain map: data (a sequence of maps), a mapping from data to dimensions, a vector of charts, labels, scales and a theme. There is no DSL and no grammar of graphics: you build and transform the map with ordinary Clojure. Statistics come from fastmath, scales from wadogo.

title: cljplot2
text:
How this book is organised

Reference - every option of the library in tables generated from its schemas: rendering, data and mapping, aesthetics and legends, scales and coordinates, layering, labels, facets and multiplots, the theme, shared option groups, errors and limits.
Use cases - one chapter per family of the R Graph Gallery merged with From Data to Viz: distribution, correlation, ranking, part of a whole, evolution, flow, and colours. Each use case has one canonical example here.
Galleries - figures replicated from other sources: cljplot extras, the lattice book, Vega-Lite and Vega galleries. Figures are reproduced by content (same data, same idea), not pixel by pixel, and link to the use case they illustrate.

Every example names its source and its dataset with the dataset’s licence. All code is Clojure written for cljplot2; no code of the original sources is copied. The datasets are in notebooks/data/ (listed in datasets.edn), not in the library.

title: cljplot2
text:
How to read an example
Each example is the code followed by the image it renders. Examples use these aliases: cljplot2.core as plot (plot/render-image returns a java.awt.image.BufferedImage, which the notebook shows) and cljplot2.chart as chart. Data is read with nu/dataset.

title: cljplot2
text:
A first example: Old Faithful
Waiting time between eruptions against eruption duration (left) and the distribution of eruption durations (right). Two plots sharing one dataset, arranged side by side.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatter, Density. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def faithful (nu/dataset :faithful))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                 :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                 :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                 :labels {:x "eruptions [min]" :y "waiting [min]"}}
                {:data faithful
                 :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/density)]
                 :labels {:x "eruptions [min]"}}]
               {:columns 2 :title "Old Faithful geyser"})
 {:width 800 :height 400})

title: 1  Reference
text:
1.1 How the part is organised
The reference lists every option of cljplot2: the plot map, render options, scales, facets, labels, the theme, every chart, builder and user-facing data function. The tables are generated from the library’s validating schemas, so they name exactly what plot/build accepts. Use cases and galleries show the options at work; this part says what exists.

title: 1  Reference
text:
Concepts (this chapter and the next eleven) - rendering, data and mapping, aesthetics and legends, scales and coordinates, layering, labels and text, facets and multiplots, the theme, the shared option groups, errors and what the library doesn’t do.
Charts, builders and data functions - the options of each chart kind, builder and user-facing function, with examples (to come; until then the use cases and galleries show them).

title: 1  Reference
text:
1.2 How to read a table
Each table is one group of related options, followed by an example using them - a chart or a value.

Option - the key; a nested key is listed after its map, with its full path (:scales :x). (required) marks a key that must be given.
Type - the values the schema accepts.
Default - the value used when the key is absent (style defaults come from the theme), and / or how a computed default is found. Empty: absent means not set - an optional feature off, or a map whose own keys have the defaults.
Description - what the key does.
Group - shown when a table mixes keys of a shared group (data and mapping, curves, strips …) with others; a group is described once, in the Shared options chapter.

title: 1  Reference
text:
1.3 A plot is a map
plot/render-image takes a plot map and render options and returns a java.awt.image.BufferedImage. The plot keys come in groups; each has its chapter.

1.3.1 Content
The rows, how their values map to dimensions, and the charts drawing them (Data and mapping chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:data
a sequence of rows (maps) or a map of columns (sequences) or nil

rows (a sequence of maps) or columns (a map of sequences) the charts read


:mapping
a mapping: key -> accessor (a keyword or a function of a row) or nil

accessors of the dimensions the charts read (keywords or functions), merged under each chart's


:charts
vector of a chart value (see cljplot2.chart) or nil

the charts, drawn in order


:groups
map

grouping options






(def points [{:x 1 :y 2 :g "a"} {:x 2 :y 3 :g "a"} {:x 3 :y 1 :g "b"} {:x 4 :y 4 :g "b"}])






x
y
g




1
2

2

a


3

b


4
4
b






(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter)]}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})




The same rows under another mapping - :x and :y swapped - give another plot:

(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :y :y :x}
                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter)]}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






1.3.2 Scales
How data values become positions, colours, shapes … (Scales and Aesthetics chapters).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:scales
map

position, facet and aesthetic scale specs






(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 12})]
                    :scales {:y {:domain [0 5] :reverse true}
                             :color {:range [:darkorange :teal] :title "group"}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})




A logarithmic x scale spreads the small values:

(plot/render-image {:data (for [i (range 1 30)] {:x (* i i i) :y i})
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :scales {:x {:kind :log :formatter :power}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






1.3.3 Coordinates
Cartesian (optionally flipped or with equal units) or polar (Scales chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:aspect
one of :iso or nil

:iso - equal pixels per data unit on x and y (linear scales)


:flip
true or false or nil
false
draw the :x scale vertically and :y horizontally


:coord
{:kind :cartesian} or a polar coord {:kind :polar ...} or nil
cartesian
coordinate system: cartesian or polar






(plot/render-image {:data [{:fruit "apples" :n 3} {:fruit "pears" :n 5} {:fruit "plums" :n 2}]
                    :mapping {:x :fruit :y :n}
                    :charts [(chart/bar)]
                    :scales {:x {:reverse true}}
                    :flip true}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})




The same bars in polar coordinates - a rose:

(plot/render-image {:data [{:fruit "apples" :n 3} {:fruit "pears" :n 5} {:fruit "plums" :n 2}]
                    :mapping {:x :fruit :y :n :color :fruit}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:width 1.0})]
                    :coord {:kind :polar}
                    :legend false}
                   {:width 350 :height 350})






1.3.4 Layout
Panels split by data, several plots in a grid, charts beside the panel (Facets chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:facets
map

facet layout: wrap shape, order, NA panel, scale relations, strips, panel weights


:custom-grid
map or nil

a hand-written layout grid instead of the generated one (only :labels {:title t} beside it)


:arrange
an arrange map {:plots :columns :rows :widths :heights :align :equal-panels} or nil

a multiplot: sub-plots in a grid (only :labels {:title t} beside it)


:margins
map

charts beside the panel sharing its scales (marginal plots)






(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :facet :g}
                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter)]}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})




A hand-written grid of plots and a note (:custom-grid, Facets chapter):

(plot/render-image {:custom-grid {:columns [{:size [:flexible 2]} {:size [:flexible 1]}]
                                  :rows [{:size [:flexible 1]} {:size [:measured]}]
                                  :items [{:id :lines :column 0 :row 0
                                           :content {:kind :plot :plot {:data points :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                                                        :charts [(chart/line)]}}}
                                          {:id :bars :column 1 :row 0
                                           :content {:kind :plot :plot {:data points :mapping {:x :g :y :y}
                                                                        :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :sum})]}}}
                                          {:id :note :column {:from 0 :to 1} :row 1
                                           :content {:kind :label :role :axis-title :text "two plots, 2 : 1"}}]}}
                   {:width 600 :height 320})






1.3.5 Titles
The plot title and the axis titles (Labels chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:labels
map

plot title and axis titles






(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/line)]
                    :labels {:title "Four points" :x "time [s]" :y "height [m]"}}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






1.3.6 Legend
Legends are drawn for mapped aesthetics; these keys hide them or draw only them (Aesthetics chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:legend
true or false or nil
true
draw the legends (false hides all)


:legend-only
true or false or nil
false
draw only the legends (a legend cell of an :arrange)






(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 12})]
                    :legend false}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






1.3.7 Style
The theme holds every style default; a plot overrides parts of it (Theme chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:alternate-panel
true or false or nil
false
shade a single panel as an odd facet panel (theme [:panel :alternate-fill])


:theme
any value

theme overrides, deep-merged over the default theme






(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter)]
                    :theme {:plot {:background :white}
                            :panel {:fill [245 245 250] :border-color [180 180 180]}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






1.3.8 Render options
Render options travel with the plot under :options; those given to render-image win (Render chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:options
map or nil

render options, merged under the ones given to build / render






(plot/render-image {:data points
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/line)]
                    :options {:width 300 :height 200}})

title: 1  Reference
text:
1.4 The pipeline
plot/build validates the plot first and throws an error listing the problems (Errors chapter). Then the plot passes through pure stages, each adding one key: :split (rows split per facet panel and group) → :stats (each chart’s computed data) → :extents → :scale-specs → :grid → :layout → :finalized-scales → :subplots. plot/render draws the result.

title: 1  Reference
text:
1.5 The tables as data
The tables come from cljplot2.describe, usable at the REPL too: describe/options takes a chart value, a builder or data function var or a schema; describe/mapping the mapping keys a chart reads; describe/theme-rows the theme; describe/fragment-rows a shared group; describe/api-vars lists the user-facing data functions, describe/chart-constructors the charts, describe/attribute-values the built-in shapes, dashes, patterns and cells. A row is a plain map; :section names its table slice:

(first (describe/options pipeline/plot-schema))


{:description
 "rows (a sequence of maps) or columns (a map of sequences) the charts read",
 :path [:data],
 :required? false,
 :key :data,
 :fragment nil,
 :default nil,
 :section :content,
 :type
 "a sequence of rows (maps) or a map of columns (sequences) or nil",
 :default-doc nil}

title: 2  Render
text:
2.1 Size and quality
Building and drawing a plot: plot/build (the built plot, data only), plot/render (a clojure2d canvas), plot/render-image (a java.awt.image.BufferedImage), plot/cvd-image (an image as seen with a colour vision deficiency) and plot/save (an image or canvas to a file). The first three take the same render options, as their second argument or under the plot’s :options (merged under the argument).
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
The image size in pixels - the whole image, legends and titles included - and the rendering quality (clojure2d hints): :low draws without antialiasing (faster, jagged edges), :mid antialiased for speed, :high antialiased for quality, :highest adds exact stroke geometry (lines can look softer).
… against :highest - smooth edges and text:

title: 2  Render
text:
Option
Type
Default
Description




:width
a positive integer
600
target width in pixels


:height
a positive integer
600
target height in pixels


:hint
one of :high :highest :low :mid
:high
rendering quality hint (antialiasing and text metrics)






(plot/render-image iris-plot {:width 500 :height 300 :hint :low})






(plot/render-image iris-plot {:width 500 :height 300 :hint :highest})

title: 2  Render
text:
2.2 Inspection
Two aids for finding out why a plot looks as it does. :debug true paints every layout item’s box under its content - panel, axes, axis titles, legend:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:debug
true or false or nil
false
paint every layout item's box (a distinct colour, its outline and id) under its content


:until
one of :split :stats :extents :scale-specs :grid :layout :finalized-scales :subplots

build stops after this pipeline stage (inspect the intermediate data)






(plot/render-image iris-plot {:width 500 :height 300 :debug true})




:until stops the build after a stage; the built plot is data. Here the build stops after :extents - the extent of each mapped dimension:

(:extents (plot/build iris-plot {:until :extents}))


{:color
 {:extent
  {:kind :categorical, :values ["setosa" "versicolor" "virginica"]},
  :na? false},
 :y
 {:extent {:kind :numeric, :min 1.0, :max 6.9},
  :padding [0.05 0.05],
  :padding-px [0.0 0.0]},
 :x
 {:extent {:kind :numeric, :min 4.3, :max 7.9},
  :padding [0.05 0.05],
  :padding-px [0.0 0.0]}}

title: 2  Render
text:
2.3 Colour vision
:cvd renders the plot as seen with a colour vision deficiency - a keyword, or [keyword severity] for the partial ones; plot/cvd-image converts any image. Red and green species, as rendered:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:cvd
a clojure2d color vision deficiency: a keyword (:protanopia, :deuteranopia, :tritanopia, :achromatopsia) or [keyword severity] (:protanomaly, :deuteranomaly, :tritanomaly, :achromatomaly; severity in [0 1]) or nil

render as seen with a colour vision deficiency






(def red-green-plot (assoc iris-plot :scales {:color {:range [[215 48 39] [26 152 80] [69 117 180]]}}))


(plot/render-image red-green-plot {:width 500 :height 300})




… and as seen with deuteranopia - setosa and versicolor turn into similar olive tones, virginica stays blue:

(plot/render-image red-green-plot {:width 500 :height 300 :cvd :deuteranopia})




A partial deficiency takes a severity in [0 1] - here deuteranomaly at half strength:

(plot/render-image red-green-plot {:width 500 :height 300 :cvd [:deuteranomaly 0.5]})

title: 2  Render
text:
2.4 Saving
plot/save writes an image (or the canvas of plot/render) to a file - the format from the extension (png, jpg, bmp, tiff …) - and returns it, so it ends a pipeline:
(-> iris-plot
    (plot/render-image {:width 800 :height 500})
    (plot/save "iris.png"))

title: 3  Data and mapping
text:
3.1 Data: rows or columns
Plot data is a sequence of maps (rows) or a map of equal-length sequences (columns). A mapping says which value of a row each dimension reads: a keyword or a function of the row. The plot’s mapping is merged under each chart’s own, and a chart reads only the keys it uses - its page lists them ((describe/mapping (chart/bar))). The mapping is open: a chart of your own may read other keys.
Columns become rows; both forms give the same plot. A chart may bring its own :data (and :mapping) - the Data and mapping group every chart takes:

title: 4  Aesthetics and legends
text:
4.1 Levels or numbers
Five aesthetics style marks from data: :color, :shape, :size, :dash and :pattern. Each mapped aesthetic has a scale (:scales {:color spec}) mapping its domain (levels or a numeric range) onto attributes (colours, shapes …), and every scale draws a legend unless told not to. All five share one spec; the colour scale uses every key, the others differ only in their :range.
Data: Gapminder 2007: life expectancy, population and GDP per capita, data-to-viz example dataset 4_ThreeNum (Yan Holtz; Gapminder via the R gapminder package); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).
An aesthetic scale has its own kinds - not those of the position scales (:log, :datetime … in the examples below are the x axis’s, Scales chapter). The kind follows the data: levels (strings, keywords) get an :ordinal scale - one attribute per level, in :domain order - numbers a :linear one - a gradient or a size range; :binned cuts numbers into classes; :type :categorical treats numbers as levels; :identity reads the attributes from the data.
Dates (java.time values) mapped to :color get a linear gradient over time, the colour bar ticked at dates:
Its :ticks take dates, and :formatter gets ticks in the data’s type (here LocalDates):

title: 4  Aesthetics and legends

Default
Description




:kind
one of :binned :identity :linear :ordinal

scale kind: :ordinal (levels), :linear (a gradient or size range), :binned (:color by bins) or :identity (values are the attributes)


:type
one of :categorical :numeric

declare numbers categorical (ordinal levels) or force a numeric scale


:domain
sequential of any value or nil
the data's levels (sorted) or [min max]
ordinal: the levels in order; linear / binned: [lo hi]

text:
4.4 Bins
A :binned colour scale cuts numbers into classes and draws a key per class. :bins takes a count of equal bins, the breaks themselves, a binning method (:sturges, :sqrt, :rice, :doane, :scott …) or quantile bins:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:bins
keyword or vector of a finite number (at least 2) or quantile bins {:quantiles q :estimation e}: q a positive count or a vector of increasing probabilities strictly between 0 and 1, e one of [:legacy :r1 :r2 :r3 :r4 :r5 :r6 :r7 :r8 :r9] or a positive integer
5 equal bins
binned :color: a bin count, breaks, a bin method or quantile bins






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [[title bins] [["3 equal bins" 3] ["breaks [39 50 60 70 83]" [39 50 60 70 83]]
                                                    ["method :sturges" :sturges] ["{:quantiles 4}" {:quantiles 4}]]]
                                   {:data gapminder
                                    :mapping {:x :gdp-per-cap :y :life-exp :color :life-exp}
                                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                                    :scales {:x {:kind :log :formatter :power}
                                             :color {:kind :binned :bins bins :range :viridis/viridis :title nil}}
                                    :labels {:title title}})
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 600})

title: 4  Aesthetics and legends
text:
4.5 Legend
One legend per mapped aesthetic, titled by the mapped column’s name: :title renames it, :formatter writes its labels, :ticks picks the entries of a numeric scale, :legend false hides it (the plot’s :legend false hides them all). Aesthetics mapped to the same column with equal levels share one legend. Legends sit right of the panels; their sizes and frame are in the theme :legend section (Theme chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:formatter
a function

legend labels, a function of the level or value


:ticks
sequential of a finite number or a java.time value or a positive integer or nil

linear :size / :color: the legend entries or colour bar ticks - a count or the values (dates for a :color scale over dates)


:title
string or nil
the mapped column's name
legend title (nil - none)


:legend
true or false or nil
true
show the scale's legend






(plot/render-image {:data gapminder
                    :mapping {:x :gdp-per-cap :y :life-exp :color :continent :shape :continent :size :pop}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :scales {:x {:kind :log :formatter :power}
                             :color {:title "continent"}
                             :size {:title "population" :ticks [1e7 1e8 1e9]
                                    :formatter #(format "%.0f M" (/ (double %) 1e6))}}}
                   {:width 700 :height 380})




A colour bar takes :ticks and :formatter too:

(plot/render-image {:data gapminder
                    :mapping {:x :gdp-per-cap :y :life-exp :color :life-exp}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :scales {:x {:kind :log :formatter :power}
                             :color {:ticks [45 55 65 75] :formatter #(str % " years") :title "life expectancy"}}}
                   {:width 600 :height 350})

title: 5  Scales, axes and coordinates
text:
5.1 Kind and domain
Position scales map :x and :y data to the panel; their kind follows the data (numbers, levels, dates) unless set. Each position scale draws an axis and grid lines. A plot is cartesian unless :coord is polar; :flip swaps the directions and :aspect :iso keeps data units square.
Data: Gapminder 2007: life expectancy, population and GDP per capita, data-to-viz example dataset 4_ThreeNum (Yan Holtz; Gapminder via the R gapminder package); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).
The scale kind (see Scale kinds below) and the data range it covers: the charts’ data extent unless :domain is given - [lo hi] for continuous kinds, the levels in order for :bands - padded (:expand) and extended to nice tick values (:nice). :type :categorical makes numbers levels (left: cylinder counts as three bands); right: fixed domains, x without padding.
Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Which kind a plot’s scales get - from the data and what the charts compute - is in the built plot’s :scale-specs: here a bar chart’s levels on x, a histogram’s bins and counts:

5.2 Ticks and labels
Where ticks go and how they read: a tick count hint or the tick values, a formatter (a function, a date pattern, :power for powers of ten), minor ticks and the tick algorithm. Minor ticks get grid lines only when the theme draws them ([:panel :grid :minor], :none by default) - turned on here:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:ticks
sequential of any value or a positive integer or nil
a count from the panel size and theme :tick-spacing
a tick count hint, or the tick values themselves


:formatter
string or one of :power or a function
the charts' suggested format, else plain numbers, levels or dates
tick label text: a function of the value, a java.time pattern (:datetime) or :power (:log)


:minor-ticks
a positive integer or nil

unlabelled ticks between two major ticks (continuous numeric kinds)


:ticks-method
one of :default :pretty
:pretty for :datetime, else :default
tick algorithm of continuous kinds: :default (d3) or :pretty (R pretty())


:ticks-params
map

tick algorithm parameters: {:min-n n}, calendar ticks {:unit u :step s}


:ticks-params :min-n
integer, >= 0

the fewest ticks (clamped to the tick count)


:ticks-params :unit
one of :days :hours :minutes :months :seconds :weeks :years

calendar tick unit (:datetime with :pretty ticks)


:ticks-params :step
a positive integer
1
a calendar tick every :step units

                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]

title: 5  Scales, axes and coordinates
text:
5.6 Scale kinds
Each kind below is described by wadogo (wadogo.scale/kind-info). cljplot2 sets a kind’s :domain (the data extent or the spec’s :domain), its :range (the panel’s pixels), ticks and tick format itself - through the options above; the remaining attributes of a kind are the “wadogo:” options.

5.6.1 Linear
:linear kind: continuous numerical domain mapped linearly to a continuous numerical range (d3 scaleLinear).
Attributes:

:domain (default [0.0 1.0]): two numbers in any order; a longer sequence is reduced to its minimum and maximum (use the :interpolated kind for piecewise mappings).
:range (default [0.0 1.0]): two numbers, reduced the same way.
:clamp (default false): when truthy, values outside the domain are constrained to it, and the inverse returns values inside the domain.
:unknown (default nil): returned for nil and NaN input.
:round (default false): when truthy, the result is rounded half up (d3 rangeRound).

Forward maps the domain ends to the range ends and extrapolates outside; inverse maps back.
Ticks are d3 style (:ticks-method :default, 10 ticks) or R pretty() style (:pretty, 5 ticks); nice extends the domain to multiples of the tick step.
A degenerate domain (equal ends) maps values below it to the range start, above it to the range end and the value itself to the middle of the range (d3 maps every value to the middle). A degenerate range behaves the same way in the inverse.

(plot/render-image {:data mtcars
                    :mapping {:x :hp :y :mpg}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})






5.6.2 Log
Positive values only; :base changes the tick values (here powers of two).
:log kind: logarithmic mapping of a positive or negative numerical domain to a continuous numerical range (d3 scaleLog).
Attributes:

:domain (default [1.0 10.0]): two numbers of the same sign; a longer sequence is reduced to its minimum and maximum. A one-value domain [x] together with :base becomes [x base].
:range (default [0.0 1.0]).
:base (default 10.0): base of the logarithm, greater than 1.0, used only by ticks and nice (the mapping doesn’t depend on it).
:clamp, :unknown, :round: as for the :linear kind.

Forward is linear in the logarithm of the absolute value; values of the other sign than the domain (and zero) give NaN.
Ticks are powers of the base and their subdivisions (d3 style, one tick per power by default) or, with :ticks-method :pretty, the grid with the tick count closest to the requested one (5 by default). nice extends the domain to the outer ticks.
A domain containing or crossing zero throws ex-info with {:domain domain}. A degenerate domain behaves as for the :linear kind.

(plot/render-image {:data (for [i (range 1 11)] {:x (Math/pow 2 i) :y i})
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter)]
                    :scales {:x {:kind :log :base 2}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})






5.6.3 Pow
:pow kind: power mapping of a continuous numerical domain to a continuous numerical range (d3 scalePow).
Attributes:

:domain (default [0.0 1.0]), :range (default [0.0 1.0]): as for the :linear kind.
:exponent (default 0.5, square root).
:clamp, :unknown, :round: as for the :linear kind.

Forward is linear in sign(x) * |x|^exponent, so negative values are mirrored. A negative exponent gives a decreasing transform, normalised back to the range ends. Exponent 0.0 maps every value, zero included, to 1.0, so the transformed domain is degenerate and every value maps to the middle of the range. Ticks and nice are linear in the domain. A degenerate domain behaves as for the :linear kind.

(plot/render-image {:data mtcars
                    :mapping {:x :hp :y :mpg}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :scales {:x {:kind :pow :exponent 0.5}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})






5.6.4 Symlog
For data of both signs over many magnitudes. The constant :C isn’t passed through (wadogo’s default 1.0).
:symlog kind: bi-symmetric logarithmic mapping of a continuous numerical domain (any sign, zero included) to a continuous numerical range (d3 scaleSymlog).
Attributes:

:domain (default [0.0 1.0]), :range (default [0.0 1.0]): as for the :linear kind.
:C (default 1.0, also for nil): the positive constant of the transform sign(x) * log(1 + |x|/C); values with |x| much smaller than C are mapped almost linearly. 0.0 gives NaN for every value, a negative C isn’t meaningful.
:base: deprecated and ignored (the base of the logarithm cancels in the mapping); kept for compatibility.
:clamp, :unknown, :round: as for the :linear kind.

Ticks and nice are linear in the domain. A degenerate domain behaves as for the :linear kind.
See: Webber, A bi-symmetric log transformation for wide-range data, Measurement Science and Technology (2013).

(plot/render-image {:data (for [i (range -40 41)] {:x (* i i i) :y i})
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :scales {:x {:kind :symlog}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})






5.6.5 Bands
Levels; the default kind for strings and keywords.
:bands kind: discrete values mapped to evenly distributed bands (intervals) of a continuous numerical range (d3 scaleBand).
Attributes:

:domain (default 1): the domain values (repeated values removed, first occurrences kept) or their count n (values 0..n-1).
:range (default [0.0 1.0]): two numbers in any order; a longer sequence is reduced to its minimum and maximum.
:padding-in (default 0.0): space between bands as a proportion of the step, constrained to [0, 1] (d3 paddingInner).
:padding-out (default 0.0): space before the first and after the last band as a proportion of the step (d3 paddingOuter), non-negative.
:align-outer (default 0.5): how the outer space is distributed: 0.0 all after the last band, 1.0 all before the first band (d3 align).
:align (default 0.5): position of the point inside every band, from 0.0 (band start) to 1.0 (band end); also :spread (positions spread from 0.0 to 1.0 over the bands) or a sequence of positions (cycled).
:round (default false): when truthy, the step is floored and the band start and width are rounded, as d3 round.
:unknown (default nil): returned for values outside the domain.

Forward returns the point of a band; with a second truthy argument it returns the band map:

:value: the domain value.
:rstart, :rend: the band ends; :rstart is the end nearer the range start, so for a reversed range :rstart is larger than :rend.
:point: the point at :align from :rstart to :rend.

The band width and the step (distance between band starts) are stored under :bandwidth and :step, the band maps under :bands in [[data]]. The inverse returns the domain value of the band containing a number (ends included), :unknown for padding and values outside the range. :padding-in is constrained to [0, 1]; 1.0 gives bands of zero width (as the :point kind). An empty domain gives no bands.
Ticks are the domain values; nice returns the scale unchanged.

(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :continent :y :n}
                    :charts [(chart/bar)]
                    :scales {:x {:align-outer 0.0 :padding-out 2.0}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})






5.6.6 Datetime
java.time values; :formatter takes a date pattern.
:datetime kind: a datetime domain mapped linearly to a continuous numerical range (d3 scaleUtc).
Attributes:

:domain (default: the year before the moment wadogo.config was loaded): two datetimes in any order, a map with :start and :end, or a longer sequence (reduced to its earliest and latest value). Accepted types: LocalDateTime, LocalDate (start of the day), LocalTime (today), java.util.Date, and Instant, ZonedDateTime and OffsetDateTime (converted to the UTC local datetime).
:range (default [0.0 1.0]): as for the :linear kind.
:clamp, :unknown, :round: as for the :linear kind.

A degenerate domain (equal ends) maps earlier datetimes to the range start, later ones to the range end and the domain datetime to the middle; it has no default ticks. A degenerate range behaves the same way in the inverse. LocalTime values are placed on the current date at each conversion, so a scale built from times shouldn’t outlive the day.
The domain is stored as LocalDateTime values. Forward accepts the same types as the domain and is linear in the elapsed time (millisecond precision with the nanosecond fraction); the inverse returns a LocalDateTime rounded to the millisecond. The domain length in milliseconds (BigDecimal, negative for a reversed domain) is stored under :millis in [[data]].
Default ticks (:ticks-method :default, 10 ticks) are spaced by a whole number of the time unit nearest to the tick step, starting at the domain start truncated to that unit, strictly inside the domain (not aligned to calendar units); :pretty ticks (5 ticks) follow R’s pretty() for date-times. Ticks of a reversed domain are reversed. Values outside the domain are extrapolated (unless clamped). nice extends the domain to whole time units (:default) or to the outer pretty ticks (:pretty).

(plot/render-image {:data (for [m (range 24)]
                            {:date (.plusMonths (LocalDate/of 2020 1 1) m) :v (+ 10 (mod (* m 7) 9))})
                    :mapping {:x :date :y :v}
                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter)]
                    :scales {:x {:formatter "MMM yyyy"}}}
                   {:width 600 :height 250})






5.6.7 Interpolated
A piecewise mapping of the domain values onto evenly spaced (or given) :stops of the panel, through an :interpolator:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:stops
sequential of a finite number (at least 2)
evenly spaced
panel fractions the :interpolated domain values map to (increasing, or decreasing - reversed)


:interpolator
a fastmath 1D interpolation method keyword or a function (fn [xs ys & params] f)
:linear
interpolation between the :stops of an :interpolated scale (only there)





:interpolated kind: piecewise mapping through (domain, range) pairs with an interpolation method.
Attributes:

:domain (default [0.0 0.5 1.0]), :range (default [0.0 0.5 1.0]): sequences of numbers of equal length, paired by position; the pairs are sorted by the domain value. Extra values of the longer sequence are dropped (also from the stored domain and range). Repeated domain values are rejected by most fastmath interpolators with ex-info when the scale is created.
:interpolator (default :linear): a fastmath.interpolation/interpolation method keyword (as :linear, :pchip, :monotone, :step) or a function of xs, ys and the parameters returning a function of one number.
:interpolator-params (default nil): a sequence of extra arguments of the interpolator, as [{:bandwidth 0.7}] for :loess.
:clamp, :unknown, :round: as for the :linear kind; the clamping interval is spanned by the smallest and the largest domain value.

A scale should be monotone: use monotone data with a monotonicity preserving method (:linear, :pchip, :monotone, step methods). :cubic, :loess, :shepard and similar can overshoot between the points.
The inverse solves forward(x) = y by bisection, so it’s the inverse of the forward curve for any monotone method. The direction (increasing or decreasing) is given by the forward values at the smallest and the largest domain value. The inverse returns the smallest domain value when forward gives y there, otherwise the smallest x with forward(x) at or beyond y (in the direction of the curve), so a plateau of a step method gives its start, and a value inside a jump gives the jump position.
Values beyond the forward values at the domain ends are searched outside the domain with growing steps, as long as the extrapolated curve keeps moving toward the value; NaN when it turns back (smooth methods extrapolate with turning polynomials), stays constant (step methods), gives NaN, or doesn’t reach the value. With :clamp such values give the nearer domain end instead.
Ticks and nice use the first and last domain value; nice replaces only these two.
The interpolators - fastmath 1D interpolation methods (or a function):

(sort schema/interpolation-methods)


(:akima
 :b-spline
 :barycentric
 :cir
 :cubic
 :cubic-smoothing
 :divided-difference
 :gp
 :kriging
 :linear
 :loess
 :microsphere-projection
 :monotone
 :neville
 :pava
 :pchip
 :polynomial
 :rbf
 :shepard
 :sprague
 :step
 :step-after
 :step-before)

Here the middle of the domain, 40 to 60, gets half of the axis:

(plot/render-image {:data (for [i (range 1 101)] {:x i :y (Math/log i)})
                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                    :charts [(chart/line)]
                    :scales {:x {:kind :interpolated :domain [1 40 60 100] :ticks [1 20 40 50 60 80 100]}}}
                   {:width 600 :height 250})






5.6.8 Radial
Radii of areas proportional to the values - for polar charts whose bar areas should read as values.
:radial kind: linear mapping of a continuous numerical domain to the squared range, so that the range values are radii of areas proportional to the domain values (d3 scaleRadial).
Attributes:

:domain (default [0.0 1.0]), :range (default [0.0 1.0]): as for the :linear kind.
:clamp, :unknown, :round: as for the :linear kind (rounding is applied to the radius).

Forward is sign(y) * sqrt(|y|) of the linear mapping of the domain to the signed squares of the range ends; inverse is its inverse. Ticks and nice are linear in the domain. Range ends of different signs are allowed (squares keep the sign). A degenerate domain maps values below it to the range start, above it to the range end and the value itself to the signed square root of the middle of the squared range.

(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :continent :y :n :color :continent}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:width 1.0})]
                    :scales {:y {:kind :radial}}
                    :coord {:kind :polar}
                    :legend false}
                   {:width 400 :height 400})

title: 5  Scales, axes and coordinates
text:
5.7 Coordinates
:flip true draws :x vertically; scales, labels and theme keys keep their names. :aspect :iso gives both linear axes the same pixels per data unit (the panel shrinks to fit). Polar coordinates map the horizontal scale to angles and the vertical one to radii.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:kind (required)
:polar

polar coordinates: the horizontal scale maps to angles, the vertical one to radii


:start
a finite number
0.0
angle of the horizontal scale's range start, degrees (0 - 12 o'clock)


:direction
one of :clockwise :counter-clockwise
:clockwise
direction of growing angles


:span
a finite number, > 0, <= 360
360.0
degrees covered (e.g. 180 for a half circle)


:inner
a finite number, >= 0, < 1
0.0
inner radius as a fraction of the outer one (a hole for donuts)


:arcs
true or false or nil
false
data lines between points follow the circle instead of chords





Polar coordinates work with these charts:

(sort (for [[kind constructor] (describe/chart-constructors)
            :when (contains? (:coords (constructor)) :polar)]
        kind))


(:bar :line :parallel :partition :rect :rule :scatter :segment :text)


(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data counts
                                   :mapping {:x :continent :y :n}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar)]
                                   :flip true
                                   :scales {:x {:reverse true}}
                                   :labels {:title ":flip true"}}
                                  {:data counts
                                   :mapping {:x :continent :y :n :color :continent}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:width 1.0})]
                                   :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.2 :span 270 :start -135}
                                   :labels {:title "polar, 270 degrees"}
                                   :legend false}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 400})

title: 6  Layering and position
text:
6.1 Layers
Charts are drawn in the order of :charts, each over the previous ones, and all of them share the plot’s scales. Grouped marks of one chart are placed by its :position option: side by side, stacked, normalized or overlaid.
A layer is any chart; annotation charts (rule, rect, text, function, image) take literal positions instead of data and inherit only the plot’s facet keys. Their extent counts for the scales unless :extent false (the Annotation options group):
Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
:extent decides whether an annotation’s positions count for the scales: a rule at 110 minutes stretches the y axis to reach it (left); with :extent false the axis keeps the data’s range and the rule is off the panel (right):

7.1 Plot labels
A plot has a title and two axis titles (:labels), each a string or a label map with its own text style. Text drawn by charts (the text chart, value labels, strip and legend texts) takes its style from a theme text role.
The plot title and the axis titles. Axis titles are absent unless given, except that statistical charts (histogram, density, ecdf, qq …) suggest one for their computed axis.

text:
7.2 Label maps
A label is a string or a label map: the text, the theme text role whose style is the base (:title for the title, :axis-title for axis titles, or a role of your theme) and a rotation. Plot labels get their role from their place; a label in a custom grid (Facets chapter) must name one. Here the y title is horizontal and styled as a tick label.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:kind
:label

content kind (labels only)


:text
any value

the text (converted with str; \n breaks lines)

keyword

theme text role styling the label (:title, :axis-title, ... or a role of your theme)


:rotation
one of 0 90 270
0
clockwise degrees (270 reads bottom to top)

title: 8  Facets, multiplots and margins
text:
8.1 Facet shape
One plot can split into panels by data (facets), several plots can share one image (plot/arrange, plot/pairs, :custom-grid), and a panel can carry charts beside it (:margins).
Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Mapping :facet wraps one panel per level into rows and columns; :facet-col / :facet-row make a grid of them. The plot’s :facets map shapes the wrap and weights the panel columns and rows.

title: 8  Facets, multiplots and margins
text:
Option
Type
Default
Description




:columns
a positive integer or nil
the most square shape (from :rows when given)
columns of a wrap layout


:rows
a positive integer or nil
the most square shape (from :columns when given)
rows of a wrap layout


:order
one of :top-down :bottom-up or nil
:top-down
wrap panel order: :top-down (first level at the top) or :bottom-up (lattice's)


:widths
sequential of a positive number (at least 1) or nil
equal
relative widths of the panel columns, one per column


:heights
sequential of a positive number (at least 1) or nil
equal
relative heights of the panel rows, one per row






(plot/render-image {:data mtcars
                    :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg :facet :carb}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :facets {:columns 4 :order :bottom-up}}
                   {:width 800 :height 400})

title: 8  Facets, multiplots and margins
text:
8.2 Facet panels
Panels share their position scales unless freed per axis (:free - each panel its data; :sliced - each panel its centre, the widest span); nil facet values get a panel of their own; strips can go.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:na-panel
true or false or nil
true
give nil facet values a panel of their own (false - drop those rows)


:scales
map

position scale relation between panels per axis


:scales :x
one of :free :same :sliced or nil
:same
x relation: :same (one domain), :free (each panel's data) or :sliced (each panel's centre, the widest span)


:scales :y
one of :free :same :sliced or nil
:same
y relation: :same (one domain), :free (each panel's data) or :sliced (each panel's centre, the widest span)


:strips
true or false or nil
true
draw the facet strips






(plot/render-image {:data mtcars
                    :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg :facet-col :cyl :facet-row :am}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :facets {:scales {:x :free} :widths [1 1 2]}}
                   {:width 800 :height 450})




:sliced: every panel spans as much as the widest one, around its own data - the panels’ y ranges are comparable in size although they sit at different heights:

(plot/render-image {:data mtcars
                    :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg :facet :cyl}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                    :facets {:scales {:y :sliced} :columns 3}}
                   {:width 800 :height 300})

8.3 Facet levels
The facet levels have scales: :scales {:facet spec} (and :facet-col / :facet-row) order the panels and write the strip texts.

title: 10  Shared options
text:
10.1 Charts
Option groups taken by several charts, builders or data functions, documented once here; other tables mark their rows with the group’s title. A chart may take only part of a group - its own table lists what it accepts.
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

title: 10  Shared options
text:
10.1.1 Data and mapping
Every chart may read its own rows and merge its own mapping over the plot’s - e.g. a reference curve beside the data (Data and mapping chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:data
a sequence of rows (maps) or a map of columns (sequences) or nil
the plot's :data
the chart's own data instead of the plot's


:mapping
a mapping: key -> accessor (a keyword or a function of a row)

the chart's mapping, merged over the plot's mapping (a key set to nil removes it)






(plot/render-image {:data wave
                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)
                             (chart/line {:data (for [t (range 0 30 0.5)] {:t t :v (Math/sin (* 0.3 t))})})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})






10.1.2 Annotation options
The rule, rect and text charts mark literal positions. By default their positions count for the scales (the axis reaches them); :extent false leaves them out - the rule at y = 2 is then off the panel (right).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:extent
true or false or nil
true
include the positions in the scale extents






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [extent [true false]]
                                   {:data wave
                                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v}
                                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/rule {:y 2 :extent extent :dash :dashed})]
                                    :labels {:title (str ":extent " extent)}})
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 250})






10.1.3 Line style
Colour, width and dash of the lines of line-like charts (line, rule, segment, smooth, density, ecdf …); a mapped aesthetic wins over the fixed value.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a clojure2d color or :none

line colour (a mapped :color wins)


:width
a non-negative number

line width in pixels


:dash
:none, a dash style (:dashed :dot-dash :dot-dot-dash :dotted :long-dash :loose-dot :solid :two-dash) or a sequence of positive numbers or nil

dash style of the line (a mapped :dash wins)






(plot/render-image {:data wave
                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v}
                    :charts [(chart/line {:color [178 34 34] :width 3 :dash [6 2]})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})






10.1.4 Curves
The line between data points of lines and ribbons: straight, a fastmath interpolation or a step, sampled for drawing.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:interpolator
a fastmath 1D interpolation method keyword or a function (fn [xs ys & params] f)

interpolation of the line between data points (none - straight segments)


:interpolator-params
vector of any value

extra parameters passed to the interpolation method


:curve
one of :parametric :bezier

path curve instead of a function of x: :parametric (x(t), y(t) over the chord length) or :bezier


:sample-step
a positive number of pixels or {:count n}, n >= 2
1.0
distance between evaluated positions: pixels or {:count n} per run






(def points (for [x (range 8)] {:x x :y (nth [1 3 2 5 4 4.5 2 3] x)}))






x
y




0
1


1
3


2
2


3
5


4
4


5
4.5


6
2


7
3






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [interpolator [:linear :monotone :cubic :step]]
                                   {:data points
                                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                    :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator interpolator}) (chart/scatter)]
                                    :labels {:title (str ":interpolator " interpolator)}})
                                 {:columns 4})
                   {:width 1000 :height 260})






10.1.5 Fill patterns
A pattern drawn over filled marks (bars, areas, boxes, tiles of hierarchies …), in its own colour.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:pattern
a pattern name (:back-hatch :cross :dense-dots :diagonal-cross :dots :hatch :horizontal :solid :vertical) or a pattern map

pattern drawn over the fill (a mapped :pattern wins)


:pattern-color
:darker or a clojure2d color or :none

pattern ink: a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill)






(plot/render-image {:data (for [[i p] (map-indexed vector [:hatch :back-hatch :cross :dots])] {:p (name p) :v (+ 3 i)})
                    :mapping {:x :p :y :v :pattern :p}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:color :white :stroke-color :black :pattern-color :black})]
                    :legend false}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})






10.1.6 Rounded corners
Rounded bar corners: all of them, or only the end away from the baseline.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:corner-radius
a non-negative number
0
radius in pixels of every bar corner


:corner-radius-end
a non-negative number

radius in pixels of the corners at the bar's value end only (wins over :corner-radius)






(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :k :y :v :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:corner-radius-end 8})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})






10.1.7 Strip placement
Strip charts (bar, box, violin, stripplot, beeswarm, dotplot, rug, bullet, extent) draw one item per level of a categorical axis. Where the items sit across the value axis, how wide, and which axis holds the levels:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:place
{:at a finite number} or one of :band :bottom :center :edge
:band with a level mapping, else the chart's own (:center for most, :edge for the rug)
where the items sit across the value axis: :band (one band per level), {:at v} (centred on v of a numeric scale), :center, :edge or :bottom (between the panel edge and 0)


:width
a non-negative number
0.8
fraction of the level's band (or of the panel for :center and :bottom) an item spans across the value axis


:thickness
a non-negative number
20 pixels for {:at v}, 8 for :edge
item thickness in pixels for :place {:at v} and :edge


:bottom-share
a number in [0 1]
0.15 with :place :bottom
padding below the data asked for with :place :bottom (only there), a fraction of the y data span


:level-axis
one of :x :y
the categorical axis of the mapping; with neither, :x when only :y is mapped, else :y
the mapping axis holding the levels (decides when both or neither of :x and :y are categorical)






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                    :charts [(chart/violin {:width 0.9}) (chart/box {:width 0.15})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 280})






10.1.8 Strip groups
Groups of one level share its band: side by side (:dodge, with a gap), on top of each other, or one half each (:mirror).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:position
one of :dodge :mirror :overlay
:dodge when a level holds two or more groups, else :overlay (dotplot: always :overlay)
how groups of one level share its band: :dodge (side by side), :overlay (on top of each other) or :mirror (two groups, one half each)


:dodge-gap
a number in [0 1]
0.1
gap between dodged groups, a fraction of a group's part of the band






(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :k :y :v :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:position :dodge :dodge-gap 0.3})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})






10.1.9 Strip counts
Each item’s row count written past its largest value.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:n-label
true or false or nil
false
draw each item's row count just past its largest value


:n-format
string
"n=%d"
format string of the n labels






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :species :y :petal-length}
                    :charts [(chart/box {:n-label true :n-format "%d flowers"})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 280})






10.1.10 Mirrored strips
Two groups on the two sides of the value axis, e.g. a population pyramid.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:mirror
one of :color :shape :size :dash :pattern :group

a grouping dimension with exactly two levels; the second level's items are drawn on the negative side






(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :k :y :v :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:mirror :color})]
                    :flip true
                    :scales {:x {:reverse true}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})






10.1.11 Ridgelines
Histograms and densities over a categorical axis - one row per level, overlapping by :overlap rows.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:overlap
a non-negative number
0.9
height of the tallest ridge in band steps (above 1 - ridges overlap the next level)






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 1.8 :fill :color :alpha 0.7})]
                    :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
                    :legend false}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






10.1.12 Cell style
The cell shape and outline of grid-cell charts (tile, bin2d): any fastmath grid type, scaled. Every cell type binning the same points:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:cell
one of :square :shifted-square :triangle :rhombus :flat-hex :pointy-hex

cell shape of the grid (a fastmath grid cell type)


:cell-scale
a finite number, > 0, <= 1

cell polygon size relative to its grid cell, in (0 1]


:stroke-color
:darker or a clojure2d color or :none

cell outline: a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill)


:stroke-width
a non-negative number

cell outline width in pixels


:alpha
a number in [0 1]

fill opacity multiplier






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [cell (:cell describe/attribute-values)]
                                   {:data iris
                                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width}
                                    :charts [(chart/bin2d {:cell cell :stroke-color :white})]
                                    :labels {:title (str ":cell " cell)}
                                    :legend false})
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 900 :height 560})






10.1.13 Field: a function
Raster and contour charts draw a scalar field: a function of a point over a domain …





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group




:f
a function

the field as a function of a point [x y] returning a number (instead of mapped data)
Fields


:domain
map
the plot's explicit :x and :y scale domains
the domain of a function field
Fields


:domain :x (required)
[a finite number, a finite number]

x domain [lo hi]



:domain :y (required)
[a finite number, a finite number]

y domain [lo hi]







(plot/render-image {:charts [(chart/contour {:f (fn [[x y]] (+ (* x x) (* 2 y y))) :domain {:x [-2 2] :y [-2 2]}})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 350})






10.1.14 Field: a density estimate
… or the kernel density estimate of mapped points …





Option
Type
Default
Description




:kernel
keyword
:gaussian
fastmath kernel of the 2D density estimate of mapped points


:bandwidth
a positive finite number or one of :nrd :nrd0 :nrd-adjust :sj :sj-dpi :rlcv :lcv :lscv :scott or [a positive finite number or one of :nrd :nrd0 :nrd-adjust :sj :sj-dpi :rlcv :lcv :lscv :scott, a positive finite number or one of :nrd :nrd0 :nrd-adjust :sj :sj-dpi :rlcv :lcv :lscv :scott]
:nrd per axis (MASS::kde2d, as ggplot2)
bandwidth of the density estimate: a number, a fastmath selector or :scott, or a pair [hx hy] of them


:binned?
true or false
false
estimate the density from binned points (faster for many points)


:cut
a non-negative finite number
3
how many bandwidths the density domain extends past the points on each side






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width}
                    :charts [(chart/field {:kernel :epanechnikov :bandwidth 0.4}) (chart/scatter {:size 3})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 350})






10.1.15 Field: the grid
… sampled on a grid of :n points per axis (interpolating gridded data with :interpolation).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:interpolation
one of :bilinear :bicubic :cubic-2d
:bilinear
interpolation of gridded data (mapped :x, :y, :value on a full lattice)


:n
integer (2..2000) or [integer (2..2000), integer (2..2000)]
100
grid size: values sampled along each axis, or [nx ny]






(plot/render-image {:charts [(chart/field {:f (fn [[x y]] (Math/sin (* x y))) :domain {:x [0 3] :y [0 3]} :n 12})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 350})






10.1.16 Hierarchy labels
Group and leaf labels of treemaps, partitions and circle packings: off, on, or a function writing them.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:group-labels
true or false or a function or nil
true
group labels: true - the node's name, false - none, or a function of the node info {:name :value :depth :path :share :parent-share} returning the text


:leaf-labels
true or false or a function or nil
true
leaf labels: as :group-labels, for the leaves






(def budget [{:dept "science" :team "physics" :cost 40} {:dept "science" :team "biology" :cost 25}
             {:dept "arts" :team "music" :cost 15} {:dept "arts" :team "theatre" :cost 10}
             {:dept "sport" :team "football" :cost 20}])

                    :mapping {:hierarchy [:dept :team] :value :cost}
                    :charts [(chart/treemap {:group-labels false :leaf-labels #(str (:name %) " " (:value %))})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






10.1.17 3D view
3D charts (cloud, surface) are seen from an eye at an azimuth and elevation, with perspective; the box has proportions and may mirror axes.





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group




:view
map

the eye's position: azimuth, elevation and perspective distance
3D frame


:view :azimuth
a finite number
40.0
rotation around the vertical axis, degrees



:view :elevation
a finite number, >= -90, <= 90
30.0
angle of the eye above the floor, degrees



:view :distance
a non-negative finite number
0.0
perspective: 0 - parallel projection, larger - stronger perspective (lattice distance)



:aspect
[a positive number, a positive number, a positive number]
[1 1 1]
box proportions [ax ay az]
3D frame


:reverse
set of one of :x :y :z

axes running the other way (mirrors the scene)
3D frame






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :z :petal-length :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/cloud {:view {:azimuth 60 :elevation 20 :distance 0.3} :aspect [1 1 0.6]})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 400})






10.1.18 3D axes
The box, the ticks and the axis titles.





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group




:box
true or false or nil
true
draw the box: hidden edges dashed and a floor grid behind the data, visible edges over it
3D frame


:axes
true or false or nil
true
draw ticks, tick labels and axis titles
3D frame


:axis-titles
map
the mapped column names
axis titles (nil - none)
3D frame


:axis-titles :x
any value

x axis title



:axis-titles :y
any value

y axis title



:axis-titles :z
any value

z axis title







(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :z :petal-length}
                    :charts [(chart/cloud {:box false :axis-titles {:x "sepal L" :y "sepal W" :z "petal L"}})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 400})






10.1.19 3D domains
Explicit domains - needed when several 3D charts share a plot.





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group




:domain
map
the data's domains
explicit data domains (needed for each of several 3D charts in one plot)
3D frame


:domain :x
[a finite number, a finite number]

explicit x domain [a b] (a > b reverses the axis)



:domain :y
[a finite number, a finite number]

explicit y domain [a b] (a > b reverses the axis)



:domain :z
[a finite number, a finite number]

explicit z domain [a b] (a > b reverses the axis)







(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :z :petal-length}
                    :charts [(chart/cloud {:domain {:x [4 8] :y [2 4.5] :z [0 7]}})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 400})






10.1.20 Text style
Font, size, colour, padding, alignment and background of the text chart - also the style of every theme text role (Theme chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:font
a bundled, installed or logical font name, or a java.awt.Font

font name (bundled, installed or logical) or a java.awt.Font


:size
a positive number

font size in points


:font-style
one of :bold :bold-italic :italic :plain

font style


:color
a clojure2d color or :contrast

text colour; :contrast - black or white by what is behind (a chart's fill under its labels, else the plot background)


:padding
a non-negative number

space around the text in pixels


:align
[h v], h one of :left :center :right, v one of :top :middle :bottom

alignment [horizontal vertical] of the text at its anchor


:background
a clojure2d color or :none

box colour behind the text (:none - no box)






(plot/render-image {:data wave
                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v}
                    :charts [(chart/line)
                             (chart/text {:x 15 :y 0 :text "a styled note" :size 14 :font-style :bold
                                          :color :white :background [70 90 140] :padding 6})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})

theme overrides of the built plot

                   {:width 500 :height 300})






10.2.2 Multiplot layout
The grid of plot/arrange (and of a plot’s :arrange): shape, weights, panel alignment.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:plots (required)
sequential of map (at least 1)

the sub-plots, filling the grid row by row

a positive integer or nil
one column (from :rows when given)
grid columns

from the plot count and :columns
grid rows

10.3 Builders and data functions
The options a builder forwards to the data function computing its layout; the function takes them directly too.

10.3.1 Graph
The edge rows’ ends, weight and node ids, optional node rows, directedness.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:from
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one
:from
accessor of an edge row's source node id


:to
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one
:to
accessor of an edge row's target node id


:value
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one
:value
accessor of an edge row's weight, a finite number >= 0 (nil - 1)


:nodes
sequential of map or nil

node rows (each with an id), placed first in their order; ids seen only in edges follow


:id
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one
:id
accessor of a node row's id


:directed?
true or false or nil
false
a directed graph: degrees split into :in and :out






(def edges [{:a "x" :b "y" :w 3} {:a "y" :b "z" :w 1} {:a "z" :b "x" :w 2} {:a "z" :b "u" :w 2}])






a
b
w




x
y
3

(plot/render-image (plot/network edges {:from :a :to :b :value :w :directed? true :labels true :rng (r/rng :mersenne 1)})
                   {:width 450 :height 300})






10.3.2 Graph layout
Node positions of a network: force-directed, a circle, or random.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:layout
one of :circle :force :random
:force
node placement: :force (Fruchterman-Reingold), :circle or :random


:iterations
integer (at least 0)
500
steps of the force layout


:gravity
a non-negative finite number
1.0
pull of the force layout to each component's centroid, in units of the ideal edge length (0 - none)


:rng
a fastmath random generator or nil
a fresh unseeded generator every call
fastmath random generator of the force and random layouts, copied per call (seeded - the same layout every time)






(plot/render-image (plot/network edges {:from :a :to :b :layout :circle :labels true}) {:width 450 :height 300})






10.3.3 Chord layout
Node order, gaps between sectors, the ring’s inner radius and the smallest drawn flow.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:order
:cluster or sequential of any value or nil
the nodes' input order
node order: a sequence of ids (those first, the rest after them in input order) or :cluster (nodes linked to the same others side by side)


:pad
a non-negative finite number
2.0
gap after every ring sector in degrees (must leave room for the sectors)


:inner
a number in (0 1)
0.92
inner radius of the ring, where the ribbons end (the outer one is 1)


:min-value
a non-negative finite number or nil

flows of a pair (summed) below it are left out and counted in :dropped (nil - none)






(plot/render-image (plot/chord flows {:pad 6 :inner 0.8}) {:width 450 :height 450})






10.3.4 Arc layout
Node order along the line.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:order
:cluster or sequential of any value or nil
the nodes' input order
node order: a sequence of ids (those first, the rest after them in input order) or :cluster (nodes linked to the same others side by side)






(plot/render-image (plot/arc edges {:from :a :to :b :order :cluster}) {:width 450 :height 250})






10.3.5 Sankey layout
Columns, node width, gaps and relaxation of a sankey diagram.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:align
one of :center :justify :left :right
:justify
the column of a node: :justify (sinks in the last column), :left, :right (by the longest path to a sink) or :center


:layer
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil
columns from :align
accessor of the node rows giving the column (integers >= 0, every edge to a later one; wins over :align)


:node-width
a number in (0 1)
0.03
node width, a fraction of the unit square's width


:pad
a non-negative finite number
0.02
least gap between the nodes of a column, a fraction of the unit square's height


:iterations
integer (at least 0)
6
relaxation sweeps moving the nodes towards their links' ends (0 - spread in the start order)


:node-sort
one of :input or nil

nil - relaxation reorders a column, :input - the input order kept






(plot/render-image (plot/sankey flows {:align :left :node-width 0.06 :pad 0.08}) {:width 500 :height 300})






10.3.6 Alluvial graph
The axes (categorical columns) the strands cross, their weights and which axis colours them.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:axes (required)
sequential of a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one (at least 2)

accessors of the axes, in column order (at least 2)


:value
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil
1 per row
accessor of a row's weight, a finite number >= 0 (nil - 1)


:fill
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil
the first axis
accessor of the level the strands are grouped (and coloured) by






(plot/render-image (plot/alluvial [{:class "1st" :sex "f" :n 140} {:class "1st" :sex "m" :n 180}
                                   {:class "3rd" :sex "f" :n 190} {:class "3rd" :sex "m" :n 510}]
                                  {:axes [:class :sex] :value :n :fill :sex})
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






10.3.7 Dendrogram layout
A cut into :k clusters and a circular layout.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:k
a positive integer or nil
no clusters (every :cluster nil)
cluster count: cutting the k - 1 highest groups leaves k subtrees, clusters 1..k in leaf order (at most the leaf count)


:circular
true or false or nil
false
radial: breadth as the angle over :span degrees, height (or depth) as the radius; points in [-1, 1]


:span
a positive finite number
360.0
degrees a circular layout covers, clockwise from the top






(def org (tree/from-levels [{:div "north" :team "a"} {:div "north" :team "b"} {:div "south" :team "c"}
                            {:div "south" :team "d"} {:div "south" :team "e"}]
                           {:hierarchy [:div :team]}))


(plot/render-image (plot/dendrogram org {:k 2}) {:width 450 :height 300})






10.3.8 Node-link tree layout
Tidy or cluster placement, diagonal or straight (:line) links, circular.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:layout
one of :tidy :cluster
:tidy
node placement: :tidy (every node at its depth, d3 tree) or :cluster (leaves at the deepest depth, d3 cluster)


:links
one of :diagonal :line
:diagonal
link shape: :diagonal (curves along the depth axis) or :line


:circular
true or false or nil
false
radial: breadth as the angle over :span degrees, height (or depth) as the radius; points in [-1, 1]


:span
a positive finite number
360.0
degrees a circular layout covers, clockwise from the top






(plot/render-image (plot/tree org {:layout :cluster :links :line}) {:width 450 :height 300})






10.3.9 Edge bundling
Edges between the tree’s leaves, bent along the tree with strength :beta.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:from
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one
:from
accessor of an edge row's source leaf id


:to
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one
:to
accessor of an edge row's target leaf id


:beta
a number in [0 1]
0.85
bundling strength: 1 - along the tree path, 0 - a straight line






(plot/render-image (plot/bundle [{:from "a" :to "d"} {:from "b" :to "e"} {:from "a" :to "c"}] org {:beta 0.9})
                   {:width 400 :height 400})






10.3.10 Sequences
Step sequences as text ("home-search-end") split into rings of a flow sunburst.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:sequence
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one
:sequence
accessor of a row's sequence: a string split at :separator or a sequence of steps


:value
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil
1 per row
accessor of a row's weight, a finite number >= 0 (nil - 1; identical sequences summed)


:separator
string
"-"
literal text splitting a string sequence into steps


:end
any value
"end"
the end marker (nil - none): a final step equal to it is removed unless :keep-end?


:keep-end?
true or false or nil
false
keep a final end marker as a step of its own (false - a sequence ending before others continue is its group's unnamed leaf)






(plot/render-image (plot/sequences [{:sequence "home-search-product" :n 5} {:sequence "home-product" :n 3}
                                    {:sequence "search-product-cart" :n 2}]
                                   {:value :n})
                   {:width 400 :height 400})






10.3.11 Autocorrelation rows
The lags of the correlogram, the significance level of its bands and which of ACF and PACF to draw.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:lags
a positive integer or nil
floor(10 log10 n), at most n - 1 (R acf)
the largest lag, from 1 to n - 1 for n values


:alpha
a number in (0 1) or nil
0.05
significance level of the band (0.05 - a 95% band)


:partial?
true or false or nil
false
the partial autocorrelation (lags from 1, a constant band) instead of the autocorrelation






(plot/render-image (plot/acf (map #(Math/sin (* 0.5 (double %))) (range 100)) {:lags 30 :partial? true})
                   {:width 600 :height 300})






10.3.12 Horizon rows
The keys of the series rows, the number and height of the bands and resampling between points.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:x
keyword or string
:x
row key of the x values (numbers)


:y
keyword or string
:y
row key of the y values (finite numbers, nil breaks the bands)


:series
keyword or string or nil
none - one series
row key of the series, one horizon per value in first-appearance order


:bands
a positive integer
2
number of bands each sign of the values is folded into


:band-height
a positive finite number or nil
the largest |y| of all series / :bands (1 when it is 0)
height of one band in y units


:interpolator
a fastmath 1D interpolation method keyword or a function (fn [xs ys & params] f) or nil
none - straight segments
a curve the valid points of every run are resampled on before folding


:steps-per-gap
a positive integer
10
resampled points per gap between consecutive x (with :interpolator)






(plot/render-image (plot/horizon (for [s ["a" "b"] t (range 60)]
                                   {:x t :y (* (if (= s "a") 1 -1) (Math/sin (* 0.2 t)) t) :series s})
                                 {:series :series :bands 3})
                   {:width 600 :height 250})

title: 11  Errors
text:
11.1 Error data
Invalid input fails before anything is computed. plot/build (and render, render-image) validates in three rounds, each throwing one ex-info listing all its errors:
Builders and data functions check their options before reading their data.
ex-data of the error: :key - the first offending key, :in - its path, :value - the value, :errors - every problem as {:in path :value v :message text}; the exception message lists the same problems as text. A misspelled key gets a spelling suggestion.
With the scale fixed, the next round reports the chart’s misspelled option:
Fixed:

title: 11  Errors
text:
(def bad-plot
  {:data [{:x 1 :y 2} {:x 2 :y 3}]
   :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
   :charts [(chart/scatter {:szie 4})]
   :scales {:x {:kind :logarithmic}}})


(try (plot/build bad-plot)
     (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e {:message (ex-message e) :data (ex-data e)}))


{:message
 "Invalid input: [:scales :x :kind] should be either :bands, :datetime, :interpolated, :linear, :log, :pow, :radial or :symlog, got :logarithmic",
 :data
 {:key :kind,
  :in [:scales :x :kind],
  :value :logarithmic,
  :errors
  [{:in [:scales :x :kind],
    :value :logarithmic,
    :message
    "should be either :bands, :datetime, :interpolated, :linear, :log, :pow, :radial or :symlog"}]}}



(try (plot/build (assoc-in bad-plot [:scales :x :kind] :log))
     (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e (ex-data e)))


{:key :szie,
 :in [:charts 0 :options :szie],
 :value 4,
 :errors
 [{:in [:charts 0 :options :szie],
   :value 4,
   :message "unknown key, should be spelled :size"}]}



(plot/render-image (-> bad-plot
                       (assoc :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})])
                       (assoc-in [:scales :x :kind] :log))
                   {:width 500 :height 300})

title: 11  Errors
text:
11.2 Builders and data functions
Options are checked against the builder’s schema before its data is read:

(try (plot/sankey [{:from "a" :to "b" :value 1}] {:node-widht 10})
     (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e (ex-data e)))


{:key :node-widht,
 :in [:node-widht],
 :value 10,
 :errors
 [{:in [:node-widht],
   :value 10,
   :message "unknown key, should be spelled :node-width"}]}

Checks of the data itself (missing columns, wrong shapes) throw the same kind of error, keyed by the option or argument at fault.

title: 11  Errors
text:
11.3 Finding the cause

:until (render options) stops the build after a stage - the built plot is data to inspect.
:debug true paints the layout boxes (Render chapter).

title: 12  Limits
text:
12.1 Output
What cljplot2 doesn’t do, and the nearest way around it.

title: 12  Limits
text: Static raster images only (BufferedImage, a clojure2d raster canvas) - no interactivity, no SVG or PDF; plot/save writes the formats Java’s ImageIO knows (png, jpg, bmp, gif, tiff …; Render chapter).

title: 12  Limits
text:
12.2 Layout

Legends sit right of the panels; there is no placement option. A legend can go elsewhere as its own plot: :legend-only true in an :arrange cell (and :legend false on the plot beside it).
No subtitle or caption: write them with the text chart in panel units, or as a title of an :arrange.
:margins need a single panel (no facets, :arrange or :custom-grid); :aspect :iso and :flip need the generated grid; free or sliced facet scales don’t combine with explicit domains or :aspect :iso.

                                                         :text "caption: synthetic data" :size 9 :extent false})]

title: 12  Limits
text:
12.3 Coordinates

Polar coordinates only with the charts declaring them (Scales, axes and coordinates chapter); no polar :aspect :iso, :margins or :custom-grid.
3D charts (cloud, surface) only with other 3D charts, without :flip, :aspect :iso, :margins, polar coordinates or free facet scales.
No map projections or geographic shapes.

title: 12  Limits
text:
12.4 Data

Data is rows (maps) or columns (equal-length sequences); other tables are converted by the caller.
Dates are java.time values; date strings stay levels.

title: 13  Distribution
text:
13.1 Violin
Charts of how the values of one numeric variable spread: violins, densities, histograms, boxplots and ridgelines (the R Graph Gallery distribution family), then beeswarms, strip plots, rugs and ECDFs.
Distribution charts put the values on :x and the groups (if any) on :y, so they are horizontal by default. :flip true draws the same plot vertically.
A violin is a kernel density estimate mirrored around the centre line of its group, here with a small box inside (the default :inner).

title: 13  Distribution
text:
13.1.1 Basic violin
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin plot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species}
  :charts [(chart/violin)]
  :labels {:title "Sepal length by species" :x "sepal length [cm]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})
