Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped, stacked and percent stacked barplot. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [p [:stack :normalize]]
         {:data diamonds
          :mapping {:x :clarity :color :cut}
          :scales {:x {:domain clarities} :color {:domain cuts}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count :position p})]
          :labels {:title (str ":position " p) :x "clarity"}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






16.1.11 Mirrored bars
:mirror turns the second level of a two-level variable the other way: back-to-back bars, with value tick labels as magnitudes. Answers for and against eight proposals, stacked by how sure people were: the mirror on :group (for / against), four colours - two blues, two reds - on :color.

(def votes
  "Seeded answers to eight proposals: people for and against, sure or leaning."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 5)]
    (vec (for [i (range 8)
               :let [support (+ 20 (r/irandom rng 60))]
               [answer share] [["for" support] ["against" (- 100 support)]]
               [certainty f] [["sure" 0.6] ["leaning" 0.4]]]
           {:proposal (str "proposal " (inc i)) :answer answer :certainty certainty
            :answer-certainty (str answer ", " certainty) :people (long (* f share 12))}))))

Source: R Graph Gallery - Barplot (back-to-back bars).

(plot/render-image
 {:data votes
  :mapping {:x :proposal :y :people :color :answer-certainty :group :answer}
  :scales {:color {:domain ["for, sure" "for, leaning" "against, sure" "against, leaning"]
                   :range {"for, sure" [8 69 148] "for, leaning" [107 174 214]
                           "against, sure" [165 15 21] "against, leaning" [251 106 74]}}}
  :charts [(chart/bar {:mirror :group :position :stack})]
  :labels {:title "For (up) and against (down), sure and leaning" :x nil :y "people"}}
 {:width 900 :height 450})






16.1.12 Economist-style labelled bars
No axes - the labels carry the values: name and value inside the bar at its base when they fit (a text chart at x = 0, in white), else just past the bar’s end. Whether a label fits is estimated here: about 7 pixels per character against the bar’s share of a 700 pixel panel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Horizontal barplot with labels (The Economist style). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [rows (mapv #(assoc % :label (str (:country %) "  " (:value %))) top-10)
      longest (double (reduce max (map :value rows)))
      fits? (fn [{:keys [value label]}] (> (* 700.0 (/ (double value) longest)) (+ 12.0 (* 7.0 (count label)))))
      text (fn [rows x anchor color] (chart/text {:data rows :mapping {:x x :y :country :label :label}
                                                  :anchor anchor :offset [6 0] :color color}))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows
    :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
    :scales {:y {:domain (ascending rows) :axis false} :x {:axis false}}
    :theme {:panel {:grid {:x :none :y :none :bands-fill :none}}}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:color [0 104 139] :stroke-color :none :width 0.7})
             (text (filterv fits? rows) (constantly 0) [:left :middle] :white)
             (text (filterv (complement fits?) rows) :value [:left :middle] [0 104 139])]
    :labels {:title {:text "Weapon exports\nTop 10 countries, value of exports" :align [:left :middle]} :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 800 :height 450}))

title: 16  Ranking
text:
16.2 Lollipop and dot plots
A thin stem and a point carry the value with less ink than a bar: chart/segment from the baseline under a chart/scatter.

16.2.1 Lollipop
Stems from 0 ((chart/segment {:xend 0})), styled stems and markers, and a baseline at the mean - stems grow both ways.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic lollipop plot; Custom lollipop chart; data-to-viz - Lollipop (1, 2, 3). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [mean (stats/mean (map :value top-20))
      base {:data top-20 :mapping {:x :value :y :country} :scales {:y {:domain (ascending top-20)}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(assoc base :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 0}) (chart/scatter)]
            :labels {:title "Basic" :x "exports" :y nil})
     (assoc base :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 0 :color [150 150 150] :width 2})
                          (chart/scatter {:size 9 :color [215 48 39] :shape \s})]
            :labels {:title "Styled stems and markers" :x "exports" :y nil})
     (assoc base :charts [(chart/rule {:x mean :dash :dashed})
                          (chart/segment {:xend mean :color [150 150 150]})
                          (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [33 102 172]})]
            :labels {:title "Baseline at the mean" :x "exports" :y nil})]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 500}))






16.2.2 Cleveland dot plot and dumbbell
Two values per item: dots alone (Cleveland), or joined by a segment from one to the other (dumbbell), ordered by the second value.

(def scores
  "Seeded scores of twelve teams in two seasons."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 11)]
    (vec (for [i (range 12)
               :let [v1 (+ 30 (r/irandom rng 50))]]
           {:team (str "team " (char (+ 65 i))) :season-1 v1 :season-2 (+ v1 -15 (r/irandom rng 35))}))))

Source: R Graph Gallery - Lollipop chart with 2 values.

(let [order (mapv :team (sort-by :season-2 scores))
      dots (fn [k color] (chart/scatter {:mapping {:x k :y :team} :size 8 :color color}))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data scores :scales {:y {:domain order}}
      :charts [(dots :season-2 [33 102 172])]
      :labels {:title "Cleveland dot plot: season 2" :x "score" :y nil}}
     {:data scores :scales {:y {:domain order}}
      :charts [(chart/segment {:mapping {:x :season-1 :xend :season-2 :y :team} :color [170 170 170] :width 2})
               (dots :season-1 [150 150 150]) (dots :season-2 [33 102 172])]
      :labels {:title "Dumbbell: season 1 (grey) to season 2 (blue)" :x "score" :y nil}}]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 450}))






16.2.3 Conditional colour and highlight
A derived column colours the lollipops above and below a threshold; a level map keeps one country in colour and greys the rest.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Lollipop chart with conditional color. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [mean (stats/mean (map :value top-20))
      rows (mapv #(assoc % :side (if (> (double (:value %)) mean) "above the mean" "below the mean")
                         :highlight (if (= "Germany (FRG)" (:country %)) "Germany (FRG)" "others"))
                 top-20)
      base {:data rows :scales {:y {:domain (ascending rows)}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(assoc base :mapping {:x :value :y :country :color :side}
            :charts [(chart/segment {:xend mean}) (chart/scatter {:size 7})]
            :labels {:title "Above / below the mean" :x "exports" :y nil})
     (assoc base :mapping {:x :value :y :country :color :highlight}
            :scales (assoc (:scales base) :color {:range {"Germany (FRG)" [215 48 39] "others" [190 190 190]}})
            :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 0}) (chart/scatter {:size 7})]
            :labels {:title "One country highlighted" :x "exports" :y nil})]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 500}))






16.2.4 Lollipop with subgroups
Items of five groups, coloured by group and ordered by value inside each group.

(def products
  "Seeded sales of six products in each of five shops."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 17)]
    (vec (for [shop ["North" "South" "East" "West" "Centre"] i (range 6)]
           {:shop shop :product (str shop " " (inc i)) :sales (+ 10 (r/irandom rng 90))}))))

Source: data-to-viz - Lollipop (subgroups).

(let [order (mapv :product (sort-by (juxt :shop :sales) products))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data products
    :mapping {:x :sales :y :product :color :shop}
    :scales {:y {:domain order}}
    :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 0}) (chart/scatter {:size 7})]
    :labels {:title "Sales of six products per shop" :x "sales" :y nil}}
   {:width 800 :height 700}))

title: 16  Ranking
text:
16.3 Circular barplot
Bars in polar coordinates: with :coord {:kind :polar} the horizontal axis goes around the circle - the levels on :x - and the vertical one along the radius; :inner leaves a hole.

16.3.1 Circular barplot: labels, order, gaps
Ordered bars with labels along their angle (:rotation :radial), and gaps between groups - blank levels in an explicit domain, their tick labels hidden by a formatter.

(def shop-groups
  "Seeded values of items in three groups."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 12)]
    (vec (for [[g n] [["A" 6] ["B" 5] ["C" 7]] i (range n)]
           {:group g :item (str g (inc i)) :value (+ 10 (r/irandom rng 90))}))))

Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic circular barplot; Labels; Circular barplot with groups; data-to-viz - Circular barplot (1, 2, 3, 4). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [levels (vec (mapcat (fn [g] (concat (map :item (filter #(= g (:group %)) shop-groups)) [(str "_" g)])) ["A" "B" "C"]))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data top-20 :mapping {:x :country :y :value}
      :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.3}
      :scales {:x {:domain (ascending top-20) :axis false} :y {:axis false :domain [0 26000]}}
      :charts [(chart/bar {:color [33 102 172] :stroke-color :none})
               (chart/text {:mapping {:x :country :y :value :label :country} :rotation :radial :size 8})]
      :labels {:title "Ordered, radial labels" :x nil :y nil}}
     {:data shop-groups :mapping {:x :item :y :value :color :group}
      :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.2}
      :scales {:x {:domain levels :formatter (fn [v] (if (= \_ (first (str v))) "" (str v)))}}
      :charts [(chart/bar)]
      :labels {:title "Gaps between groups" :x nil :y nil}}]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 500}))






16.3.2 Stacked and dodged circular bars
The bar positions work around the circle too.

(def parts
  "Seeded values of three parts of twelve items."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 23)]
    (vec (for [i (range 12) part ["x" "y" "z"]]
           {:item (str "item " (inc i)) :part part :value (+ 5 (r/irandom rng 30))}))))

Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular stacked barplot.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [p [:stack :dodge]]
         {:data parts :mapping {:x :item :y :value :color :part}
          :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.15}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position p})]
          :labels {:title (str ":position " p) :x nil :y nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






16.3.3 Circular lollipop
Segments and points in polar coordinates: the levels on the angle (:x), the values on the radius - on a log scale (stems from 50), so the small values don’t crowd the centre.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular barplot. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [order (rseq (ascending top-20))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data top-20 :mapping {:x :country :y :value}
    :coord {:kind :polar :start -9}
    :scales {:x {:domain (vec order)} :y {:kind :log}}
    :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 50 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 8 :color [215 48 39]})]
    :labels {:title "Weapon exports, top 20" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 600 :height 600}))

title: 16  Ranking
text:
16.4 Parallel coordinates
Each row a line across one axis per variable (chart/parallel over :variables); every axis has its own scale in the variable’s units, drawn by the chart.

(def iris-variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width])


16.4.1 Parallel coordinates: groups, highlight, vertical
Lines coloured by species; a level map greys all but one species; :flip true stacks the axes vertically.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Parallel coordinates chart with ggally; data-to-viz - Parallel coordinates (1, 2). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data iris :mapping {:color :species}
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables})]
    :labels {:title "By species" :x nil}}
   {:data iris :mapping {:color :species}
    :scales {:color {:range {"setosa" [190 190 190 120] "versicolor" [190 190 190 120] "virginica" [215 48 39 220]}}}
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables})]
    :labels {:title "Virginica highlighted" :x nil}}
   {:data iris :mapping {:color :species} :flip true
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables})]
    :labels {:title "Vertical (:flip true)" :x nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})






16.4.2 Smooth connections
:curve :smooth joins the axes with curves that meet every axis flat, at its value, and never overshoot; :smoothness (0..1) moves the bend toward the axes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Parallel plot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[title opts] [["Straight" {}] [":curve :smooth" {:curve :smooth}]]]
         {:data (take-nth 3 iris) :mapping {:color :species} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/parallel (merge {:variables iris-variables} opts))]
          :labels {:title title :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






16.4.3 Scaling
:scaling - per variable (v - offset) / scale: :std (mean, sd), :robust (median, R’s mad), :uniminmax (every axis 0..1, the default), :globalminmax (the values as they are, one scale).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Parallel coordinates chart with ggally (scaling). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [scaling [:std :robust :uniminmax :globalminmax]]
         {:data iris :mapping {:color :species} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables :scaling scaling :width 0.5})]
          :labels {:title (str ":scaling " scaling) :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 700})






16.4.4 Axis order
The axes follow :variables: neighbours are compared, so the order changes what the chart shows.
Source: data-to-viz - Parallel coordinates (axis order). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[title vs] [["Measured order" iris-variables]
                          ["Sepal width beside the petals" [:sepal-width :petal-length :sepal-length :petal-width]]]]
         {:data iris :mapping {:color :species} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables vs})]
          :labels {:title title :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})

title: 16  Ranking
text:
16.5 Radar
A radar (spider) chart is chart/parallel in polar coordinates: variables on angles, values along the spokes, each row a closed polygon - filled with :fill.

(def car-variables [:mpg :hp :wt :qsec :drat :disp])


(def four-cars (filterv #(#{"Mazda RX4" "Merc 240D" "Lotus Europa" "Cadillac Fleetwood"} (:model %)) mtcars))


(def car-limits
  "Every variable's range over all 32 cars."
  (into {} (map (fn [k] [k [(reduce min (map k mtcars)) (reduce max (map k mtcars))]])) car-variables))


16.5.1 Radar: groups and limits
Four cars filled; the same cars on axes fixed to the range of all cars (:limits); all cars by cylinders on standardized axes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic radar chart; Radar chart with several individuals (1, 2). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [(plot/arrange
    [{:data four-cars :mapping {:color :model} :coord {:kind :polar} :legend false
      :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables car-variables :fill :color :width 2})]
      :labels {:title "Four cars, their own ranges" :x nil}}
     {:data four-cars :mapping {:color :model} :coord {:kind :polar}
      :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables car-variables :fill :color :width 2 :limits car-limits})]
      :labels {:title "Ranges of all 32 cars (:limits)" :x nil}}]
    {:columns 2 :widths [2 3]})
   {:data (map #(assoc % :cylinders (str (long (:cyl %)))) mtcars) :mapping {:color :cylinders} :coord {:kind :polar}
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables car-variables :scaling :std})]
    :labels {:title "All cars by cylinders (:std)" :x nil}}]
  {:columns 1 :heights [1 1]})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})






16.5.2 Variables as rings
With :flip true the variables become rings and the values angles: every flower is a line from ring to ring - the species separate on the petal rings and mix on sepal width.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Spider / radar chart. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:color :species}
  :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.25} :flip true
  :scales {:color {:range {"setosa" [27 158 119 110] "versicolor" [217 95 2 110] "virginica" [117 112 179 110]}}}
  :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables :width 0.8})]
  :labels {:title "150 iris flowers across four rings" :x nil}}
 {:width 750 :height 700})

title: 16  Ranking
text:
16.6 Bump
A bump chart shows ranks over time - see Evolution - Bump chart (levels/rank-rows, monotone lines, end labels).

title: 16  Ranking
text:
16.7 Caveats

16.7.1 Order the data
Unordered categories make the reader sort them; ordered by value, the ranking is read at a glance - here all 38 countries with a value, as lollipops on a log scale (exports from 2 to 12394; the stems start at 1, as log 0 is undefined).
Source: data-to-viz - Order your data. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[title y-scale] [["Alphabetical" {}] ["Ordered by value" {:domain (ascending weapons)}]]]
         {:data (alphabetical weapons) :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
          :scales {:x {:kind :log} :y y-scale}
          :theme {:axis {:y {:label-gap 1}}}
          :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 1 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 5 :color [33 102 172]})]
          :labels {:title title :x "exports (log scale)" :y nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})






16.7.2 Barplot or histogram
A barplot shows a value per category; a histogram shows how one numeric variable is distributed - bins of a continuous axis, no gaps.
Source: data-to-viz - Barplot; Histogram (1, 2). Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data diamonds :mapping {:x :cut} :scales {:x {:domain cuts}}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count})] :labels {:title "Barplot: diamonds per cut" :x nil :y "count"}}
   {:data diamonds :mapping {:x :price}
    :charts [(chart/histogram)] :labels {:title "Histogram: diamond prices" :x "price, USD"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






16.7.3 Radar: the order of the axes
The same car in two axis orders: the polygon’s shape and area change with the order, though the values don’t.
Source: data-to-viz - Spider chart caveats. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [vs [car-variables [:mpg :wt :hp :drat :qsec :disp]]]
         {:data (filter #(= "Mazda RX4" (:model %)) mtcars) :coord {:kind :polar}
          :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables vs :fill :color :width 2 :limits car-limits})]
          :labels {:title (str "Mazda RX4: " (str/join " " (map name vs))) :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






16.7.4 Circular bars exaggerate the outer ones
Around a circle an outer bar is longer than an inner bar of the same value, and the angle of each bar hides its length: the straight bars compare honestly.
Source: data-to-viz - Circular barplot y axis. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data top-10 :mapping {:x :country :y :value} :scales {:x {:domain (ascending top-10)}}
    :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.2}
    :charts [(chart/bar)] :labels {:title "Circular" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:data top-10 :mapping {:x :country :y :value} :scales {:x {:domain (ascending top-10)}}
    :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -45}}}
    :charts [(chart/bar)] :labels {:title "Straight" :x nil :y "exports"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.1 Grouped and stacked bars
How a whole splits into parts: grouped and stacked bars, treemaps, donuts and pies, circle packing, sunbursts, waffles, Venn diagrams and UpSet plots (the R Graph Gallery part-of-a-whole pages, the data-to-viz sunburst and the pie caveat).
Not here: dendrograms wait for hierarchical clustering in fastmath (backlog); the sunburst of flows belongs to the Flow chapter.
Bars of groups within categories: side by side, on top of each other, scaled to the whole, or one panel per category.

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.1.1 Grouped, stacked, percent
R Graph Gallery’s specie × condition values (seeded): :dodge compares the groups, :stack the totals, :normalize the shares; facets give a panel per specie; negative values stack downward from 0.

(def species-conditions
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 42)]
    (vec (for [specie ["banana" "poacee" "sorgho" "triticum"]
               condition ["normal" "stress" "Nitrogen"]]
           {:specie specie :condition condition :value (m/abs (r/grandom rng 0.0 15.0))}))))


(def signed-conditions
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 7)]
    (mapv #(assoc % :value (r/grandom rng 0.0 15.0)) species-conditions)))

Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped and Stacked barplot.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (concat
        (for [[title position legend?] [["grouped (:dodge)" :dodge false] ["stacked (:stack)" :stack false]
                                        ["percent (:normalize)" :normalize true]]]
          {:data species-conditions :mapping {:x :specie :y :value :color :condition} :legend legend?
           :charts [(chart/bar {:position position})]
           :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})
        [{:data species-conditions :mapping {:x :condition :y :value :facet :specie}
          :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -90}}}
          :charts [(chart/bar)]
          :labels {:title "small multiples" :x nil :y nil}}
         {:data signed-conditions :mapping {:x :specie :y :value :color :condition}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack})]
          :labels {:title "negative values" :x nil :y nil}}]))
  {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 650})






17.1.2 Likert scale
Survey answers as diverging stacked bars (seeded counts): disagreement to the left of 0, agreement to the right, the neutral answers split half to each side (two :groups of one colour). :negative-order :reverse stacks the negative side from the last answer, so the answers in their natural order diverge from the middle.

(def answers ["Strongly disagree" "Disagree" "Neutral" "Agree" "Strongly agree"])


(def likert
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 3)]
    (vec (for [q (range 1 6)
               [i answer] (map-indexed vector answers)
               :let [n (+ 5 (r/irandom rng 40))
                     sign ({0 -1.0 1 -1.0 3 1.0 4 1.0} i)]
               row (if sign
                     [{:question (str "Q" q) :answer answer :side "" :count (* sign n)}]
                     ;; the neutral answer: half on each side, two groups of one colour
                     [{:question (str "Q" q) :answer answer :side "-" :count (* -0.5 n)}
                      {:question (str "Q" q) :answer answer :side "+" :count (* 0.5 n)}])]
           row))))

Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped and Stacked barplot (the Likert package).

(plot/render-image
 {:data likert :mapping {:x :count :y :question :color :answer :group :side}
  :scales {:color {:domain answers
                   :range {"Strongly disagree" [178 24 43] "Disagree" [239 138 98] "Neutral" [200 200 200]
                           "Agree" [103 169 207] "Strongly agree" [33 102 172]}}
          :x {:formatter #(str (long (m/abs (double %))))}}
  :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :negative-order :reverse})]
  :labels {:title "Five questions, five answers" :x "answers" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 380})

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.2 Treemap
Nested rectangles, areas proportional to the value: the world’s population by region, subregion and country.

17.2.1 Basic, groups and subgroups
One level (regions) and three (regions → subregions → countries); :padding frames the groups, a theme palette recolours the regions.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Treemap; data-to-viz - Treemap (1, 2). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region]} :charts [(chart/treemap)]
    :labels {:title "regions"}}
   {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]}
    :theme {:palette {:color :set2}}
    :charts [(chart/treemap {:padding 4 :border-color [60 60 60]})]
    :labels {:title "regions, subregions, countries (:set2, :padding 4)"}}]
  {:columns 2 :widths [1 2]})
 {:width 1000 :height 520})






17.2.2 Annotated treemap
Label functions get the node’s name, value, depth and shares: the countries with their population in millions.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Treemap (annotations, labels and colors). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :country]}
  :charts [(chart/treemap {:leaf-labels #(format "%s\n%.0f M" (:name %) (/ (double (:value %)) 1e6))
                           :group-labels #(format "%s - %.1f%%" (:name %) (* 100.0 (double (:share %))))})]
  :labels {:title "World population (millions)"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 700})

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.3 Donut
A ring of stacked shares: the regions’ populations around a hole (:inner - the hole’s radius as a fraction).

17.3.1 Basic, labels, ring thickness
Source: R Graph Gallery - Donut chart; data-to-viz - Donut (1, 2). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [inner [0.3 0.7]]
         (assoc pie-base
                :coord {:kind :polar :inner inner}
                :scales {:x {:axis false}}
                :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label percent-label})]
                :labels {:title (str ":inner " inner) :x nil :y nil})))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






17.3.2 Half donut
:span 180 from :start -90: the circle shrinks to a half and fits its panel; outer labels name the parts.
Source: data-to-viz - Donut (variations). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (assoc pie-base
        :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.5 :span 180 :start -90}
        :legend false
        :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label share-label :label-position :outer})]
        :labels {:title "World population by region" :x nil :y nil})
 {:width 800 :height 420})

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.4 Pie
A donut without its hole. data-to-viz: angles are hard to compare - see the caveat at the end.

17.4.1 Basic, colours, a clean pie
The default pie shows its value axis around the circle - the cumulative population, here in billions; a palette recolours it; :axis false cleans it up.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Pie chart. Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [(assoc pie-base :legend false :scales {:x {:formatter #(format "%.0fB" (/ (double %) 1e9))}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0})] :labels {:title "default (axis in billions)" :x nil :y nil})
   (assoc pie-base :theme {:palette {:color :MetBrewer/Archambault}} :legend false
          :scales {:x {:formatter #(format "%.0fB" (/ (double %) 1e9))}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0})] :labels {:title ":MetBrewer/Archambault" :x nil :y nil})
   (assoc pie-base :scales {:x {:axis false}} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :stroke-color :white :stroke-width 1})]
          :labels {:title "clean" :x nil :y nil})]
  {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 380})






17.4.2 Slice labels
Label functions get each slice’s value, count and share: shares inside the slices, or names and shares outside with leader lines (:label-position :outer - the angle axis gives way, the circle makes room).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Pie chart (labels). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [(assoc pie-base :scales {:x {:axis false}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label percent-label})]
          :labels {:title "inside" :x nil :y nil})
   (assoc pie-base :legend false
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label share-label :label-position :outer
                               :label-leader true})]
          :labels {:title "outside, with leaders" :x nil :y nil})]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 480})

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.5 Circle packing
Circles with areas proportional to the value, nested in their groups’ enclosing circles - a group’s area isn’t proportional to its value (packing leaves gaps), compare circles within a group.

17.5.1 One level
Europe’s countries: a circle each (the palette’s colours repeat - they only tell neighbours apart); leaves coloured by their subregion; wider gaps (:padding, pixels).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular packing; data-to-viz - Circular packing (1, 2). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data europe :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:country]} :legend false
    :charts [(chart/pack)] :labels {:title "basic"}}
   {:data europe :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:country] :color :subregion}
    :charts [(chart/pack {:padding 6 :leaf-labels false})] :labels {:title "by subregion, :padding 6"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 480})






17.5.2 Several levels
Regions → subregions → countries: the regions’ colours lighter at every level, group names under their circles’ tops.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular packing (several levels). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]}
  :charts [(chart/pack)] :labels {:title "Regions, subregions, countries"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 800})




Hiding the regions (:hidden-levels #{1}) leaves the subregions floating - the layout stays the same.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular packing (hide some levels). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]}
  :charts [(chart/pack {:hidden-levels #{1}})] :labels {:title "Regions hidden"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 800})

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.6 Sunburst
The hierarchy as rings: a partition (an icicle in cartesian coordinates) under polar coordinates - regions inside, subregions, then countries outward.
Source: data-to-viz - Sunburst. Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]} :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.15}
    :charts [(chart/partition)] :labels {:title "sunburst"}}
   {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion]}
    :charts [(chart/partition)] :labels {:title "icicle (two levels)"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 520})

title: 17  Part of a whole
text:
17.7 Waffle
A grid of cells: by default 10 × 10, a cell per percent of the whole (largest-remainder rounding keeps the total at 100).

17.7.1 Basic, shapes, colours, groups
The regions’ shares; circle cells; a palette; subregions within each region (a facet per region, each region’s subregions in shades of one colour - 22 subregions are more than a palette’s 20 colours).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Waffle chart. Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data world :mapping {:color :region :value :population} :charts [(chart/waffle)] :labels {:title "regions"}}
   {:data world :mapping {:color :region :value :population} :theme {:palette {:color :dark2}}
    :charts [(chart/waffle {:shape :circle :gap 0.15})] :labels {:title "circles, :dark2"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})




Source: R Graph Gallery - Waffle chart (groups and subgroups). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(def subregion-colors
  "Each region's subregions in shades of the region's colour (darker to lighter)."
  (into {} (for [[base [_ subregions]] (map vector (c/palette :category10)
                                             (sort-by key (group-by :region (nu/dataset :world-population))))
                 :let [names (sort (distinct (map :subregion subregions)))]
                 [i subregion] (map-indexed vector names)]
             [subregion (c/brighten base (- (* 0.7 (double i)) 1.0))])))


(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:color :subregion :value :population :facet :region}
  :scales {:color {:range subregion-colors}}
  :charts [(chart/waffle {:gap 0.15})]
  :labels {:title "Subregions within each region"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 520})

title: 17  Part of a whole
17  Part of a whole
text:
17.9 Caveats

17.9.1 The issue with pie charts
data-to-viz: three sets of five nearly equal values. As pies the differences hide in the angles; as bars they read at once. (3D pies, exploded slices and legends far from the slices make it worse - not drawn here.)

(def caveat-data
  {"data 1" [17 18 20 22 24] "data 2" [20 18 21 20 20] "data 3" [24 23 21 19 18]})


(defn- caveat-rows [values] (mapv (fn [part v] {:part part :value v}) ["a" "b" "c" "d" "e"] values))


#'use-cases.part-of-a-whole/caveat-rows

Source: data-to-viz - The issue with pie chart.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (concat
        (for [[title values] caveat-data]
          {:data (caveat-rows values) :mapping {:x :value :color :part} :coord {:kind :polar} :scales {:x {:axis false}}
           :legend false :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0})] :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})
        (for [[title values] caveat-data]
          {:data (caveat-rows values) :mapping {:x :part :y :value :color :part} :legend false
           :charts [(chart/bar)] :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})))
  {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 650})






17.9.2 Other caveats

Circle packing: only leaf areas follow the values - a group’s circle also holds the gaps between its children.
Treemaps: label at most three levels; deeper ones get too small to read (data-to-viz).
Sunbursts and donuts compare angles, as pies do; outer rings exaggerate the deeper levels (their arcs are longer for the same share).


source: notebooks/use_cases/part_of_a_whole.clj

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.1 Scatter
How two or more variables move together: scatter plots, heatmaps, correlograms, bubble charts, connected scatter plots, 2D densities, functions of two variables and the ways out of overplotting (the R Graph Gallery correlation pages and data-to-viz).
Not here: labels along a trend line and label repel, clustered heatmap order with dendrograms (waits for hierarchical clustering in fastmath), arrows on connected scatter plots (backlog), 3D densities and interactivity.
One point per observation at its two values; colour, shape and size carry more variables.

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.1.1 Basic scatter, styled points
Living area against sale price of 1460 houses: the default points, then a translucent fill with an outline and another shape.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic scatterplot with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Scatter (1, 2). Data: House prices: living area and sale price, data-to-viz example dataset 2_TwoNum (Yan Holtz; Kaggle House Prices competition); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data houses :mapping {:x :living-area :y :price} :charts [(chart/scatter)]
    :labels {:title "default" :x "living area, sq ft" :y "price, USD"}}
   {:data houses :mapping {:x :living-area :y :price}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:shape \A :size 6 :color [70 130 180 90] :stroke-color [20 60 100] :stroke-width 0.5})]
    :labels {:title "translucent triangles with outlines" :x "living area, sq ft" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






18.1.2 Colour and shape by group
Mapping :color and :shape to the same variable gives every species its colour and shape, and one legend.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Map a variable to a ggplot2 scatterplot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species :shape :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})]
  :labels {:title "Iris sepals by species" :x "sepal length, cm" :y "sepal width, cm"}}
 {:width 700 :height 500})






18.1.3 Text labels in boxes
A text chart names some cars; :background puts each label on a semi-transparent box, so the points it covers stay visible and the text stays readable over them.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Add text labels with ggplot2. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [label-box {:size 9 :background [255 255 255 200] :padding 2 :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg :label :model}}]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8 :color [200 60 40]})
             (chart/text (merge label-box {:data (filterv #(> (double (:mpg %)) 31.0) mtcars)
                                           :anchor [:left :middle] :offset [6 0]}))
             (chart/text (merge label-box {:data (filterv #(or (> (double (:wt %)) 5.3) (> (double (:hp %)) 250.0)) mtcars)
                                           :anchor [:right :middle] :offset [-6 0]}))]
    :labels {:title "Cars by weight and fuel use" :x "weight, 1000 lbs" :y "miles per gallon"}}
   {:width 750 :height 500}))






18.1.4 Rugs and marginal distributions
Margins share the panel’s axes: rugs (one line per value) beside both axes, or the densities of both variables.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Marginal distribution with ggplot2. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})]
  :margins {:top {:charts (chart/rug) :size 25} :right {:charts (chart/rug) :size 25}}
  :labels {:title "Old Faithful with rugs" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
 {:width 650 :height 480})





(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})]
  :margins {:top (chart/density {:fill [70 130 180 120]}) :right (chart/density {:fill [70 130 180 120]})}
  :labels {:title "Old Faithful with marginal densities" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
 {:width 650 :height 520})






18.1.5 Linear fit with a confidence band
chart/smooth {:method :lm} adds the least-squares line and its 95 % confidence band.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatterplot with a regression line. Data: House prices: living area and sale price, data-to-viz example dataset 2_TwoNum (Yan Holtz; Kaggle House Prices competition); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data houses :mapping {:x :living-area :y :price}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [0 0 0 70]}) (chart/smooth {:method :lm})]
  :labels {:title "Price grows with living area" :x "living area, sq ft" :y "price, USD"}}
 {:width 700 :height 480})






18.1.6 A scatter per group
A facet mapping draws one panel per species on shared scales.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Faceting with ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :facet :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 5})]
  :labels {:title "Iris sepals, a panel per species" :x "sepal length, cm" :y "sepal width, cm"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






18.1.7 Size by overlap count
Integer data puts many cars on one point; counting the cars per point and mapping the count to the point’s area (:area true on the size scale) shows how many sit there.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatterplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [counts (mapv (fn [[[cyl gear] cars]] {:cyl cyl :gear gear :cars (count cars)})
                   (group-by (juxt :cyl :gear) mtcars))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data counts :mapping {:x :cyl :y :gear :size :cars}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:color [70 130 180 200]})]
    :scales {:size {:area true :range [4 36] :title "cars"}}
    :labels {:title "Cars per cylinder and gear count" :x "cylinders" :y "forward gears"}}
   {:width 650 :height 450}))






18.1.8 Manhattan plot
A genome-wide association plot (seeded data): one point per marker at its position along the chromosomes and its −log10 p-value, chromosomes in alternating colours and numbered at their centres (explicit :ticks with a :formatter), the significance threshold 5·10⁻⁸ as a rule.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Manhattan plot.

(def markers
  "Seeded association results: 22 chromosomes of 200-400 markers, uniform p-values with three peaks."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 101)
        peaks {3 0.4 9 0.7 16 0.3}]
    (loop [chromosome 1 offset 0.0 rows []]
      (if (> chromosome 22)
        rows
        (let [n (r/irandom rng 200 400)
              chromosome-rows (for [i (range n)
                                    :let [t (/ (double i) n)
                                          peak (get peaks chromosome)
                                          strength (if peak (* 9.0 (m/exp (- (m/sq (/ (- t peak) 0.03))))) 0.0)
                                          p (* (r/drandom rng) (m/pow 10.0 (- strength)))]]
                                {:chromosome chromosome :position (+ offset i) :log-p (- (m/log10 (max p 1.0e-12)))})]
          (recur (inc chromosome) (+ offset n) (into rows chromosome-rows)))))))


(let [centres (into (sorted-map) (for [[chromosome rows] (group-by :chromosome markers)]
                                     [(stats/mean (map :position rows)) chromosome]))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data markers :mapping {:x :position :y :log-p :color #(if (odd? (:chromosome %)) "odd" "even")}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3})
             (chart/rule {:y (- (m/log10 5.0e-8)) :dash :dashed :color [200 40 40]})]
    :scales {:x {:ticks (vec (keys centres)) :formatter #(str (get centres (double %)))}
             :color {:range {"odd" [40 70 120] "even" [140 170 210]} :legend false}}
    :theme {:panel {:grid {:x :none}}}
    :labels {:title "Association with a trait along 22 chromosomes" :x "chromosome" :y "-log10 p"}}
   {:width 1000 :height 400}))






18.1.9 Simpson’s paradox
Three groups (seeded): within each group y grows with x, across all of them it falls. One fit for everything points the wrong way; a fit per group shows the relation inside the groups.
Source: data-to-viz - Simpson’s paradox.

(def simpson
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 33)]
    (vec (for [[g cx cy] [["A" 2.0 9.0] ["B" 5.0 6.0] ["C" 8.0 3.0]]
               _ (range 40)
               :let [dx (r/grandom rng 0.0 1.0)]]
           {:group g :x (+ cx dx) :y (+ cy (* 0.8 dx) (r/grandom rng 0.0 0.5))}))))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data simpson :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 5 :color [90 90 90]}) (chart/smooth {:method :lm})]
    :labels {:title "one fit: y falls with x"}}
   {:data simpson :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :group}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 5}) (chart/smooth {:method :lm})]
    :theme {:palette {:color :set1}}
    :labels {:title "a fit per group: y grows with x" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 430})

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.2 Heatmap
A grid of cells coloured by a value: rows and columns are categories (or binned numbers).

18.2.1 Basic heatmap, square and hexagon cells
European countries × demographic indicators, each indicator standardized (z-score) so the colours compare across columns of different units; :cell :pointy-hex draws the same grid as a honeycomb.

(def europe (filterv #(= "Europe" (:continent %)) countries))

Source: R Graph Gallery - Heatmap; data-to-viz - Heatmap (1, 2). Data: Countries: demographic indicators, data-to-viz example dataset multivariate (Yan Holtz; original source not documented); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [rows (z-scores europe)
      heatmap (fn [cell title legend?]
                {:data rows :mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :z} :legend legend?
                 :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
                 :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation 90}}}
                 :charts [(chart/tile {:cell cell})]
                 :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(heatmap :square "square cells" false) (heatmap :pointy-hex "pointy-hex cells" true)]
                 {:columns 1})
   {:width 1000 :height 800}))






18.2.2 Palettes, normalized columns
Raw values put every indicator on one colour scale, so life expectancy (around 80) drowns the rates (0-20); standardizing each column first gives every indicator the full palette. Any palette or gradient works: viridis on the left, a diverging RdBu around 0 on the right.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Heatmap with the levelplot function. Data: Countries: demographic indicators, data-to-viz example dataset multivariate (Yan Holtz; original source not documented); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [rows (z-scores (take 25 europe))
      base {:data rows :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation 90}}} :labels {:x nil :y nil}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(merge base {:mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :value} :charts [(chart/tile)]
                  :scales {:color {:range :viridis :title "value"}}
                  :labels {:title "raw values (viridis)" :x nil :y nil}})
     (merge base {:mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :z} :charts [(chart/tile)]
                  :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
                  :labels {:title "standardized per indicator (RdBu)" :x nil :y nil}})]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 520}))






18.2.3 Side colour bar
A category of the columns as a one-row tile above the heatmap: both plots share the column order (:domain), plot/arrange aligns the cells. Here: up to six of the most populous countries of each continent (the dataset has two in North America), grouped by continent.
Source: R Graph Gallery - The heatmap function (side colours). Data: Countries: demographic indicators, data-to-viz example dataset multivariate (Yan Holtz; original source not documented); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [picked (vec (mapcat (fn [[_ rows]] (take 6 (sort-by #(- (double (:pop %))) rows)))
                          (sort-by key (group-by :continent countries))))
      order (mapv :country picked)]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data picked :mapping {:x :country :y (constantly "continent") :color :continent}
      :scales {:x {:domain order :axis false} :color {:title "continent"}}
      :charts [(chart/tile {:stroke-color :white})]
      :labels {:title "Indicators of the largest countries per continent" :x nil :y nil}}
     {:data (z-scores picked) :mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :z}
      :scales {:x {:domain order} :color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
      :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation 90}}}
      :charts [(chart/tile {:stroke-color :white})]
      :labels {:x nil :y nil}}]
    {:columns 1 :heights [1 6]})
   {:width 1000 :height 600}))






18.2.4 Values in cells: the correlation matrix
fastmath.stats/correlation-matrix gives r of every pair of variables; one tile per pair, coloured on a diverging scale over [-1 1] and labelled with its value (:value-label, text in a contrasting colour).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlation matrix with ggally (heatmap). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [variables [:mpg :cyl :disp :hp :drat :wt :qsec :gear :carb]
      names (mapv name variables)
      r (stats/correlation-matrix (mapv (fn [k] (mapv k mtcars)) variables))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (vec (for [i (range (count names)) j (range (count names))]
                 {:x (names i) :y (names j) :r (nth (nth r i) j)}))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :r}
    :scales {:y {:domain (vec (reverse names))} :color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :domain [-1 1] :title "r"}}
    :charts [(chart/tile {:stroke-color :white :value-label (fn [{:keys [value]}] (format "%.2f" (double value)))})]
    :labels {:title "mtcars: correlation of every pair" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 700 :height 600}))






18.2.5 Calendar heatmap
Daily bitcoin price changes on a calendar: ISO week across, weekday down, a row of panels per year; the colour is the day’s change, capped at ±10 % so a few extreme days don’t flatten the rest.
Source: R Graph Gallery - The hourly heatmap (calendar layout). Data: Bitcoin daily price, 2013-2018, data-to-viz example dataset 3_TwoNumOrdered (Yan Holtz; CoinMarketCap via JesseVent/crypto); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [weekdays ["Mon" "Tue" "Wed" "Thu" "Fri" "Sat" "Sun"]
      days (vec (for [[prev day] (partition 2 1 bitcoin)
                      :let [^LocalDate d (:date day)]]
                  {:week (.get d IsoFields/WEEK_OF_WEEK_BASED_YEAR)
                   :year (.get d IsoFields/WEEK_BASED_YEAR)
                   :weekday (weekdays (dec (.getValue ^DayOfWeek (.getDayOfWeek d))))
                   :change (m/constrain (- (/ (double (:value day)) (double (:value prev))) 1.0) -0.1 0.1)}))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data days :mapping {:x :week :y :weekday :color :change :facet-row :year}
    :scales {:y {:domain (vec (reverse weekdays))}
             :color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdYlGn :midpoint 0 :domain [-0.1 0.1] :title "daily change"
                     :formatter #(format "%+.0f%%" (* 100.0 (double %)))}}
    :charts [(chart/tile {:stroke-color :white})]
    :labels {:title "Bitcoin: daily price change, 2013-2018" :x "ISO week" :y nil}}
   {:width 1000 :height 800}))






18.2.6 Row and column order
The order of the categories is the scale’s :domain: the data order (the default; here the dataset’s subregions) hides structure that a meaningful order shows - countries sorted by life expectancy.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Heatmap. Data: Countries: demographic indicators, data-to-viz example dataset multivariate (Yan Holtz; original source not documented); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [rows (z-scores europe)
      by-life (mapv :country (sort-by :life-expectancy europe))
      heatmap (fn [order title legend?]
                {:data rows :mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :z} :legend legend?
                 :scales (cond-> {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
                           order (assoc :x {:domain order}))
                 :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation 90}}}
                 :charts [(chart/tile)]
                 :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(heatmap nil "data order" false) (heatmap by-life "by life expectancy" true)] {:columns 1})
   {:width 1000 :height 800}))






18.2.7 Smoothed heatmap
Measurements on a coarse lattice (seeded: two bumps and noise) as tiles, and the same values interpolated bicubically into a smooth field with contour lines.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density chart (raster smoothing).

(def lattice
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 21)]
    (vec (for [x (range 12) y (range 9)]
           {:x x :y y :z (+ (* 8 (m/exp (- (/ (+ (m/sq (- x 3)) (m/sq (- y 6))) 6.0))))
                            (* 5 (m/exp (- (/ (+ (m/sq (- x 8)) (m/sq (- y 2))) 8.0))))
                            (* 0.6 (r/drandom rng)))}))))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data lattice :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :z} :charts [(chart/tile)] :legend false
    :labels {:title "measured lattice"}}
   {:data lattice :mapping {:x :x :y :y :value :z}
    :charts [(chart/field {:interpolation :bicubic}) (chart/contour {:interpolation :bicubic :color [0 0 0 120]})]
    :labels {:title "bicubic field and contours" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 430})

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.3 Correlogram
All pairs of several variables at once: plot/pairs lays out a matrix of cells sharing the variables’ scales.

18.3.1 Scatter-plot matrix by group
Scatter plots below the diagonal, densities on it, the correlation per species above it, coloured by species.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlogram; data-to-viz - Correlogram (1, 2). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/pairs iris {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width] :mapping {:color :species}
                   :theme {:palette {:color :set1}} :title "Iris measurements by species"})
 {:width 950 :height 800})






18.3.2 Correlation glyphs
chart/correlation draws r of its cell as a glyph: ellipses (the shape of a bivariate normal with that r) below, pies (|r| as a filled angle) above, the variable names on the diagonal; the r colour bar on the side.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlation ellipses. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/pairs mtcars {:variables [:mpg :disp :hp :drat :wt :qsec]
                     :lower (chart/correlation {:glyph :ellipse}) :upper (chart/correlation {:glyph :pie})
                     :diagonal :names :title "mtcars correlogram"})
 {:width 800 :height 750})

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.4 Bubble
A scatter plot with a third variable as the point’s size - by area, so a point twice the value has twice the ink.

18.4.1 Bubble chart: area, size range, colours and legend
Gapminder 2007: income (log axis) against life expectancy, population as the bubble’s area (:area true, size range 1-40 px), continent as colour. The left panel maps population linearly to the diameter: large countries look far larger than they are.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Bubble chart; data-to-viz - Bubble (1, 2). Data: Gapminder 2007: life expectancy, population and GDP per capita, data-to-viz example dataset 4_ThreeNum (Yan Holtz; Gapminder via the R gapminder package); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [bubbles (fn [area? title legend?]
                {:data (sort-by #(- (double (:pop %))) gapminder) :legend legend?
                 :mapping {:x :gdp-per-cap :y :life-exp :size #(/ (double (:pop %)) 1.0e6) :color :continent}
                 :scales {:x {:kind :log} :size (cond-> {:range [1 40] :title "population, M"} area? (assoc :area true))}
                 :charts [(chart/scatter {:stroke-color :white :stroke-width 0.5})]
                 :theme {:palette {:color :set2}}
                 :labels {:title title :x "GDP per capita, USD" :y "life expectancy, years"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(bubbles false "diameter linear in population" false) (bubbles true "area linear in population" true)]
                 {:columns 2 :widths [1 1.25]})
   {:width 1000 :height 480}))

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.5 Connected scatter
Two variables over time: the points in time order joined by a path, dates written next to some of them.

18.5.1 Connected scatter with dates
Yearly means of US unemployment duration and savings rate, 1990-2014; labels on boxes keep the years readable where the path crosses itself.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Connected scatterplot with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Connected scatter (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [yearly (vec (for [[year rows] (sort-by key (group-by #(.getYear ^LocalDate (:date %)) economics))
                        :when (<= 1990 year 2014)]
                    {:year year :uempmed (stats/mean (map :uempmed rows)) :psavert (stats/mean (map :psavert rows))}))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data yearly :mapping {:x :uempmed :y :psavert}
    :charts [(chart/line {:sort false :curve :bezier :color [33 102 172]})
             (chart/scatter {:size 6 :color [33 102 172]})
             (chart/text {:data (filterv #(zero? (mod (long (:year %)) 4)) yearly)
                          :mapping {:x :uempmed :y :psavert :label :year}
                          :background [255 255 255 210] :padding 2 :anchor [:left :bottom] :offset [5 5]})]
    :labels {:title "Unemployment duration vs savings rate, 1990-2014" :x "median unemployment, weeks" :y "savings rate, %"}}
   {:width 800 :height 550}))

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.6 2D density
Where the points concentrate: counts in cells, a smooth density estimate, its contour lines.

18.6.1 2D histogram and hexbin
chart/bin2d counts points in cells: squares, or hexagons (the default) - regular on screen for the panel’s shape.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density chart; data-to-viz - 2D density (1, 2). Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/bin2d {:cell :square :bins 20})]
    :legend false :labels {:title "2D histogram" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
   {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins 20})]
    :labels {:title "hexbin" :x "eruption, min" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






18.6.2 2D kernel density and contours
chart/field estimates the density (Gaussian kernel, a bandwidth per axis) and draws it as a raster; chart/contour draws its level lines, or with :fill true the bands between them.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density plot with ggplot2. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
    :charts [(chart/field) (chart/contour {:color :white :width 0.8})] :legend false
    :labels {:title "density raster and contour lines" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
   {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
    :charts [(chart/contour {:fill true :levels 8})]
    :labels {:title "filled contour bands" :x "eruption, min" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






18.6.3 Points over a density
The density as a backdrop for the points themselves.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density chart. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
  :charts [(chart/field {:alpha 0.8}) (chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [255 255 255 200]})]
  :labels {:title "Old Faithful eruptions over their density" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
 {:width 700 :height 500})

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.7 Functions
chart/field {:f f} samples a function of a point [x y] on a grid over a given domain (:n samples per axis) - no data needed. These examples have no gallery counterpart.

18.7.1 A function as a raster
−(x² + y²) · sin x · sin y · sin xy on [−π, π]², white to black, 300 × 300 samples, square pixels (:aspect :iso).
Source: cljplot2 - chart/field.

(defn fn2d
  [[x y]]
  (let [x (double x) y (double y)]
    (* (- (+ (* x x) (* y y))) (m/sin x) (m/sin y) (m/sin (* x y)))))


(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:f fn2d :domain {:x [(- m/PI) m/PI] :y [(- m/PI) m/PI]} :n 300})]
  :scales {:color {:range [:white :black]}}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "-(x^2 + y^2) sin x sin y sin xy"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






18.7.2 A function with contour lines
sin x · cos y on a diverging palette centred at 0, with contour lines at fixed levels.
Source: cljplot2 - chart/field, chart/contour.

(let [wave (fn [[x y]] (* (m/sin x) (m/cos y)))
      domain {:x [0 (* 2 m/PI)] :y [0 4]}]
  (plot/render-image
   {:charts [(chart/field {:f wave :domain domain})
             (chart/contour {:f wave :domain domain :color :black :levels [-0.75 -0.5 -0.25 0 0.25 0.5 0.75]})]
    :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :title "sin x cos y"}}
    :labels {:title "sin x cos y with contour lines"}}
   {:width 700 :height 450}))

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.8 Overplotting
With thousands of points a scatter plot turns into a blot. The usual ways out, on 53 940 diamonds.

18.8.1 Size, transparency, sampling, binning, facets, margins
Smaller points and transparency let density show; a sample keeps the shape with fewer points; hexagon counts replace points by numbers; facets split the cloud by a category; marginal densities show where it is thick.
Source: data-to-viz - Overplotting. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [base {:data diamonds :mapping {:x :carat :y :price} :scales {:x {:domain [0 5.5] :nice false :expand [0 0]} :y {:domain [0 20000] :nice false :expand [0 0]}}}
      sample (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 9)] (filterv (fn [_] (< (r/drandom rng) 0.04)) diamonds))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter)] :labels {:title "all points" :x "carat" :y "price, USD"}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter {:size 1})] :labels {:title "small points" :x "carat" :y nil}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [30 60 120 12]})] :labels {:title "transparency" :x "carat" :y nil}})
     (merge base {:data sample :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [30 60 120 120]})]
                  :labels {:title "4 % sample" :x "carat" :y "price, USD"}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins 30})] :legend false :labels {:title "hexbin" :x "carat" :y nil}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter {:size 2 :color [30 60 120 20]})]
                  :margins {:top (chart/density {:fill [30 60 120 100]}) :right (chart/density {:fill [30 60 120 100]})}
                  :labels {:title "marginal densities" :x "carat" :y nil}})]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 700}))




Source: data-to-viz - Overplotting (facets). Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diamonds :mapping {:x :carat :y :price :facet :cut}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 2 :color [30 60 120 25]})]
  :scales {:facet {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}
  :labels {:title "Diamonds: a panel per cut, worst to best" :x "carat" :y "price, USD"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






18.8.2 Jitter
Integer values pile up on a few positions; :jitter [dx dy] moves every point by a random offset within ±dx, ±dy (data units) so the piles spread - :rng with a seed makes it the same in every rendering.
Source: data-to-viz - Overplotting (jitter). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [gears (fn [title jitter]
              {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :cyl :y :gear}
               :charts [(chart/scatter (cond-> {:size 7 :color [40 40 40 120]}
                                         jitter (assoc :jitter jitter :rng (r/rng :mersenne 7))))]
               :labels {:title title :x "cylinders" :y "forward gears"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(gears "32 cars on 8 positions" nil) (gears ":jitter [0.25 0.15]" [0.25 0.15])] {:columns 2})
   {:width 900 :height 420}))

title: 18  Correlation
text:
18.9 Caveats

18.9.1 Anscombe’s quartet
Four datasets with the same means, variances, linear fit and r ≈ 0.82 - and four different relations: a line, a curve, a line with an outlier, a single far point making the correlation. Always look at the scatter plot. The same mean and spread of x and the same residual variance give the same line and confidence band; drawn over the whole x domain (:full-range with an explicit :domain, shared by the panels) they coincide.
Source: Anscombe (1973), Graphs in Statistical Analysis (R datasets::anscombe).

(def anscombe
  "Anscombe's quartet (R `datasets::anscombe`) in long form."
  (let [x123 [10 8 13 9 11 14 6 4 12 7 5]
        x4 [8 8 8 8 8 8 8 19 8 8 8]
        ys {"I" [8.04 6.95 7.58 8.81 8.33 9.96 7.24 4.26 10.84 4.82 5.68]
            "II" [9.14 8.14 8.74 8.77 9.26 8.10 6.13 3.10 9.13 7.26 4.74]
            "III" [7.46 6.77 12.74 7.11 7.81 8.84 6.08 5.39 8.15 6.42 5.73]
            "IV" [6.58 5.76 7.71 8.84 8.47 7.04 5.25 12.50 5.56 7.91 6.89]}]
    (vec (for [set ["I" "II" "III" "IV"] [x y] (map vector (if (= "IV" set) x4 x123) (ys set))]
           {:set set :x x :y y}))))


(let [r-label (fn [rows] (format "r = %.2f" (stats/pearson-correlation (map :x rows) (map :y rows))))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data anscombe :mapping {:x :x :y :y :facet :set}
    :facets {:columns 4}
    :scales {:x {:domain [3 20]}}
    :charts [(chart/smooth {:method :lm :full-range true})
             (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [200 60 40]})
             (chart/text {:data (vec (for [[set rows] (group-by :set anscombe)] {:set set :x 4 :y 13 :label (r-label rows)}))
                          :mapping {:x :x :y :y :label :label} :anchor [:left :top]
                          :background [255 255 255 210] :padding 3})]
    :labels {:title "Anscombe's quartet: one r, four relations"}}
   {:width 1000 :height 330}))






18.9.2 Other caveats

Correlation is not causation: two variables can move together because a third one drives both.
Pearson’s r measures only a linear relation: very different clouds (Anscombe’s quartet) share one r; look at the scatter plot, and use Spearman or Kendall (chart/correlation {:method :spearman}) for monotone relations.
Bubbles: map the value to the area (:area true), not the diameter, or large values look far larger.
2D histograms and densities depend on the cell size or bandwidth: try a few before reading shapes into them.


source: notebooks/use_cases/correlation.clj

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.1 Chord diagram
Connections and flows between entities: chord diagrams, networks, sankey and alluvial diagrams, bump charts, arc diagrams, hierarchical edge bundling, dendrograms, clustered heatmaps, circular plots and flow sunbursts (the R Graph Gallery flow pages and data-to-viz). Every layout is a function returning rows, drawn by ordinary charts; the plot/... builders return plain plot maps.
Not here: interactivity, multi-track circular plots, gradient ribbons and links, cyclic sankeys, crossing minimization beyond clustering, arcs below the line and label repel.
Flows between groups around a circle: a ring sector per group, sized by its flow, and a ribbon per link.

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.1.1 Chord diagram from an edge list
Migration between ten world regions: directed - a ribbon per flow, as wide as the flow at both ends, the sectors holding the flows out and in - and undirected, a ribbon per pair of regions, as wide as their exchange.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Chord diagram; data-to-viz - Chord diagram (1, 2). Data: Migration flows between world regions, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyDirectedWeighted (long form; Yan Holtz, after Abel & Sander 2014); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [(plot/chord migration {:directed? true :min-value 0.1 :title "directed flows"})
                (plot/chord migration {:min-value 0.1 :title "exchange between regions"})]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 520})






19.1.2 Colours, gaps, order and weak links
:min-value drops the weak flows that clutter the middle, :pad widens the gaps, :order :cluster puts regions with similar partners side by side, and the palette is a plot scale like any other.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Advanced chord diagram with circlize; data-to-viz - Chord diagram (1, 2). Data: Migration flows between world regions, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyDirectedWeighted (long form; Yan Holtz, after Abel & Sander 2014); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/chord migration {:directed? true :min-value 0.5 :pad 4 :order :cluster
                        :scales {:color {:range :category10}}
                        :title "Flows of at least 0.5 million, clustered order"})
 {:width 700 :height 700})

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.2 Network
Nodes and the edges between them, placed by a layout; colour, size and width carry node and edge variables.

19.2.1 From an adjacency table
Co-authorships between researchers come as a table - a row per author, a column per author, 1 for a joint paper. The table isn’t square, so its cells become edge rows directly (graph/adjacency->edges reads square matrices, see the correlation network below); the force layout places them, seeded for a stable picture. Groups of authors without joint papers between them are laid out apart and packed in rows, the largest first.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Input formats for network charts; data-to-viz - Network (1, 2). Data: Co-authorships between researchers, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyUndirectedUnweighted (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(def coauthor-edges
  "One edge per co-author pair (the table lists some pairs both ways)."
  (->> (nu/dataset :coauthors)
       (mapcat (fn [{:keys [from] :as row}]
                 (for [[k v] (dissoc row :from) :when (= 1 v)] (vec (sort [from (name k)])))))
       (remove (fn [[a b]] (= a b)))
       (distinct)
       (mapv (fn [[a b]] {:from a :to b}))))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/network coauthor-edges {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 11) :node-style {:size 8}
                               :title (str (count coauthor-edges) " co-authorships")})
 {:width 750 :height 700})






19.2.2 Layouts
The same graph on a circle and with the Fruchterman-Reingold force layout: groups of characters that appear together only come out of the force layout.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Network layouts; data-to-viz - Network (1, 2). Data: Les Misérables character co-occurrences, vega-datasets miserables.json (D. E. Knuth, The Stanford GraphBase, 1993); licence: Not specified (vega-datasets lists it as notspecified).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (vec (for [[layout title] [[:circle "circle layout"] [:force "force layout"]]]
                      (plot/network co-occurrences {:nodes characters :layout layout :rng (r/rng :mersenne 3)
                                                    :mapping {:color :group} :scales {:color {:legend false}}
                                                    :title title})))
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






19.2.3 Node colour, size by degree
Nodes coloured by their group and sized by their number of links (:degree, computed with the graph); labels for the main characters. One size scale serves one variable, so edge widths (below, for migration flows) and node sizes don’t go together.
Source: R Graph Gallery - igraph plotting parameters, map a colour, node size by edges number (1, 2, 3). Data: Les Misérables character co-occurrences, vega-datasets miserables.json (D. E. Knuth, The Stanford GraphBase, 1993); licence: Not specified (vega-datasets lists it as notspecified).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/network co-occurrences {:nodes characters :rng (r/rng :mersenne 3)
                               :mapping {:color :group :size :degree}
                               :scales {:size {:title "links"}}
                               :labels #(when (>= (long (:degree %)) 10) (:id %))
                               :title "Les Misérables: characters appearing together"})
 {:width 900 :height 750})






19.2.4 Correlation network
Variables linked when their correlation is strong (|r| > 0.7): the matrix becomes edges with graph/adjacency->edges, the weight is |r| and the colour its sign.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlation network with igraph. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def correlation-edges
  (let [names (mapv name mtcars-variables)
        r (stats/correlation-matrix (mapv (fn [k] (mapv k mtcars)) mtcars-variables))
        strong (mapv (fn [row] (mapv #(if (> (Math/abs (double %)) 0.7) % 0) row)) r)]
    (mapv #(assoc % :r (:value %) :value (Math/abs (double (:value %))))
          (graph/adjacency->edges strong names {:directed? false}))))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/network correlation-edges {:nodes (mapv (fn [k] {:id (name k)}) mtcars-variables) :rng (r/rng :mersenne 5)
                                  :labels true
                                  :edge-mapping {:color #(if (pos? (double (:r %))) "positive" "negative")}
                                  :scales {:color {:range {"positive" [33 102 172] "negative" [178 24 43]} :title "r"}}
                                  :title "mtcars variables with |r| > 0.7"})
 {:width 700 :height 600})






19.2.5 Directed, weighted edges
Migration flows as arrows ending at the target’s edge, edge widths from the flows’ size scale.
Source: data-to-viz - Network. Data: Migration flows between world regions, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyDirectedWeighted (long form; Yan Holtz, after Abel & Sander 2014); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/network migration {:directed? true :layout :circle :labels true
                          :edge-mapping {:size :value}
                          :scales {:size {:range [0.5 6] :title "migrants, M"}}
                          :title "Migration between world regions"})
 {:width 750 :height 650})

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.3 Sankey
Flows through stages: nodes in columns, as tall as their flow, bands between them as wide as the flow.

19.3.1 Sankey diagram, node and link colours
The UK energy flows of a 2050 scenario: sources on the left, uses on the right (:align :justify, the default), bands in their source’s colour; then every node as far left as it can go, bands in their target’s colour.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Sankey diagram with networkD3, custom colours; data-to-viz - Sankey (1, 2, 3). Data: UK energy flows in 2050 (a DECC scenario), networkD3 JSONdata/energy.json (the d3 sankey example; UK Department of Energy & Climate Change 2050 Calculator); licence: networkD3 is GPL-3; the data’s licence isn’t stated.

(def energy-flows (nu/dataset :energy))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/sankey energy-flows {:title "UK energy flows in 2050 (TWh)"})
 {:width 1000 :height 650})





(plot/render-image
 (plot/sankey energy-flows {:align :left :link-color :target :title "Left-aligned, bands in the target's colour"})
 {:width 1000 :height 650})






19.3.2 Alluvial diagram
A column per variable, a stratum per level and strands between neighbouring columns, coloured by the class all the way through.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Sankey diagram (alluvial section). Data: Titanic passengers and crew by class, sex, age and survival, R datasets package Titanic (Dawson 1995); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/alluvial (nu/dataset :titanic) {:axes [:class :sex :age :survived] :value :n :fill :class
                                       :theme {:palette {:color :set1}}
                                       :title "Titanic: 2201 people by class, sex, age and survival"})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






19.3.3 Bump chart
Ranks over time: the months ranked by passengers within each year. The summer months climb to the top as air travel grows; November stays near the bottom.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Sankey diagram (bump chart section). Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def month-ranks
  (vec (for [[year rows] (group-by :year air-passengers)
             [rank row] (map-indexed vector (sort-by :passengers > rows))]
         (assoc row :rank (inc rank)))))


(plot/render-image
 {:data month-ranks :mapping {:x :year :y :rank :color :month}
  :charts [(chart/line {:width 2})
           (chart/scatter {:size 7})
           (chart/text {:data (filter #(= 1949 (:year %)) month-ranks) :mapping {:x :year :y :rank :label :month}
                        :anchor [:right :middle] :offset [-8 0]})
