           (chart/text {:data (filter #(= 1960 (:year %)) month-ranks) :mapping {:x :year :y :rank :label :month}
                        :anchor [:left :middle] :offset [8 0]})]
  :scales {:y {:domain [12.5 0.5] :nice false :ticks (vec (range 1 13))}
           :x {:domain [1948 1961] :nice false :ticks (vec (range 1949 1961))}
           :color {:domain ["Jan" "Feb" "Mar" "Apr" "May" "Jun" "Jul" "Aug" "Sep" "Oct" "Nov" "Dec"]
                   :range :category20 :legend false}}
  :labels {:title "Months ranked by air passengers, 1949-1960" :x nil :y "rank"}}
 {:width 900 :height 550})

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.4 Arc diagram
Nodes on a line, every link a semicircle above it: readable when the order puts linked nodes close together.
Source: data-to-viz - Arc diagram. Data: Les Misérables character co-occurrences, vega-datasets miserables.json (D. E. Knuth, The Stanford GraphBase, 1993); licence: Not specified (vega-datasets lists it as notspecified).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [(plot/arc co-occurrences {:nodes characters :mapping {:color :group}
                                          :title "Les Misérables: input order"})
                (plot/arc co-occurrences {:nodes characters :mapping {:color :group} :order :cluster
                                          :title "clustered order: characters seen with the same others together"})]
               {:columns 1})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.5 Edge bundling
Links between the leaves of a hierarchy routed along it: the bundles show which packages depend on which.

19.5.1 Hierarchical edge bundling
The classes of the flare library around a circle, grouped by package, each import a curve through the package tree, coloured by the importing class’s top-level package.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Hierarchical edge bundling, custom, labels; data-to-viz - Edge bundling (1, 2, 3, 4). Data: Flare visualization toolkit class hierarchy, vega-datasets flare.json (the Flare ActionScript library’s packages and classes); licence: Not documented.

(def flare-tree (tree/from-parents (nu/dataset :flare) {:name :name}))


(def flare-imports (nu/dataset :flare-dependencies))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/bundle flare-imports flare-tree {:from :source :to :target
                                        :title "flare: class imports bundled along the package tree"})
 {:width 800 :height 800})






19.5.2 Bundling strength
:beta straightens the curves: 0 draws straight lines, 1 follows the tree exactly.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Custom hierarchical edge bundling. Data: Flare visualization toolkit class hierarchy, vega-datasets flare.json (the Flare ActionScript library’s packages and classes); licence: Not documented.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (vec (for [beta [0.0 0.5 1.0]]
                      (plot/bundle flare-imports flare-tree {:from :source :to :target :beta beta :labels? false
                                                             :scales {:color {:legend false}}
                                                             :title (str ":beta " beta)})))
               {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 380})

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.6 Dendrogram
A hierarchy as a tree of branches: from data with levels, or from hierarchical clustering, where the height of a merge is the distance between the groups.

19.6.1 From hierarchical data
World regions and their subregions, the tree drawn from the levels of the rows.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dendrogram with ggraph; data-to-viz - Dendrogram (1, 2). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/dendrogram (tree/from-levels (nu/dataset :world-population) {:hierarchy [:region :subregion]})
                  {:horizontal true :group-labels? true :title "World regions and subregions"})
 {:width 650 :height 650})






19.6.2 From clustering, coloured clusters, circular
Complete-linkage clustering of the standardized cars (fastmath hclust), cut into 3 clusters; the same tree around a circle.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic dendrogram, custom colours, circular dendrogram, dendextend (1, 2, 3, 4). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def car-clustering (cl/hclust standardized {:method :complete}))


(def cars (mapv :model mtcars))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/dendrogram car-clustering {:labels cars :k 3 :theme {:palette {:color :set1}}
                                  :title "mtcars: complete-linkage clustering, 3 clusters"})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})





(plot/render-image
 (plot/dendrogram car-clustering {:labels cars :k 3 :circular true :theme {:palette {:color :set1}}
                                  :title "The same clustering, circular"})
 {:width 700 :height 700})

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.7 Clustered heatmap
Rows and columns of a heatmap ordered by clustering, their dendrograms beside it: similar cars and similar variables come together.
Source: R Graph Gallery - The heatmap function. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/clustered-heatmap (vec (for [[car row] (map vector cars standardized) [k v] (map vector mtcars-variables row)]
                                {:car car :variable (name k) :z v}))
                         {:row :car :col :variable :value :z
                          :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
                          :title "mtcars: cars and variables ordered by clustering"})
 {:width 900 :height 800})

title: 19  Flow
19  Flow
text:
19.9 Flow sunburst
Sequences of steps (website visits, here 2000 synthetic sessions) as rings from the centre: every step coloured by its page wherever it occurs, end where a session stops.
Source: data-to-viz - Sunburst.

(def pages ["home" "search" "product" "account" "cart" "help"])


(def visits
  "2000 sessions starting at home: each step to another page or the end (more likely the longer the session), at
  most 6 pages; a seeded random walk."
  (let [g (r/rng :mersenne 7)
        weights {"home" [0 5 3 2 0 1] "search" [1 2 6 0 1 1] "product" [1 2 2 1 4 1]
                 "account" [2 0 1 1 1 2] "cart" [0 0 2 2 0 1] "help" [2 2 0 2 0 1]}
        pick (fn [ws] (let [total (double (reduce + ws)) u (* total (r/drandom g))]
                        (loop [i 0 acc 0.0]
                          (let [acc (+ acc (double (ws i)))]
                            (if (or (< u acc) (= i (dec (count ws)))) i (recur (inc i) acc))))))]
    (vec (for [_ (range 2000)]
           {:sequence (str/join "-" (loop [path ["home"]]
                                      (if (or (= 6 (count path)) (< (r/drandom g) (* 0.12 (count path))))
                                        (conj path "end")
                                        (recur (conj path (pages (pick (weights (peek path)))))))))}))))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/sequences visits {:scales {:color {:domain (conj pages "end")}}
                         :title "2000 website visits: pages in order from the centre"})
 {:width 700 :height 650})

title: 19  Flow
text:
19.10 Caveats

A network of many nodes and links becomes a hairball: filter weak links, or show the graph as an arc diagram or an adjacency heatmap instead.
Order changes the reading of chord and arc diagrams: :order :cluster puts nodes with the same partners together; input order may scatter them.
Weak links clutter chord and sankey diagrams; :min-value leaves them out (and the layout says how many).
Sankey diagrams show flows that go one way: a flow back to an earlier node is a cycle the layout refuses.
Widths and areas encode values: a band twice as wide is twice the flow, a sector twice as long twice the total.

Source: data-to-viz - Caveats: spaghetti plot, order your data (1, 2).

source: notebooks/use_cases/flow.clj

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.1 Statistics
The examples of the original cljplot - its sketches and the showcase images of its README - rebuilt with cljplot2. Styling differs from the originals; the chart types and what they show are the same. Data are the originals’ where available (Old Faithful, Seattle weather), otherwise synthetic and seeded.
Not here: the image mosaics, the animation, and the lattice and Vega examples (their own galleries).

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.1.1 Q-Q plot
Quantiles against quantiles: a sample against a distribution (:x-distribution), per group with a quartile line each; then two distributions against each other, no data at all, labelled for the legend.
Source: cljplot - qqplot.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 1)
      sample (vec (concat (for [_ (range 300)] {:v (r/grandom g) :group "normal"})
                          (for [_ (range 300)] {:v (r/sample (r/distribution :t {:degrees-of-freedom 3 :rng g})) :group "t(3)"})))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [{:data sample :mapping {:y :v :color :group}
                   :charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal]})]
                   :labels {:title "samples against the normal" :y "sample quantiles"}}
                  {:charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal] :y-distribution [:t {:degrees-of-freedom 3}]
                                       :label "t(3)" :mapping {:color :label}})
                            (chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal] :y-distribution [:t {:degrees-of-freedom 30}]
                                       :label "t(30)" :mapping {:color :label} :line false})]
                   :labels {:title "t distributions against the normal"}}]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 450}))




Two groups against each other: one column per group (the shorter padded with nils, which the chart drops), the longer one interpolated.
Source: cljplot - qqplot. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [faithful (nu/dataset :faithful)
      short-wait (map :eruptions (filter #(< (double (:waiting %)) 70.0) faithful))
      long-wait (map :eruptions (filter #(>= (double (:waiting %)) 70.0) faithful))
      rows (take (max (count short-wait) (count long-wait))
                 (map (fn [a b] {:short a :long b}) (concat short-wait (repeat nil)) (concat long-wait (repeat nil))))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows :mapping {:x :short :y :long}
    :charts [(chart/qq)]
    :labels {:title "Old Faithful eruptions: after short against after long waits" :x "waiting < 70 min" :y "waiting >= 70 min"}}
   {:width 550 :height 500}))






20.1.2 P-P plot
Probabilities against probabilities: a t sample’s empirical CDF against the normal CDF, y = x for reference.
Source: cljplot - ppplot.

(let [d (r/distribution :t {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 2)})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 2000 (fn [] {:v (r/sample d)}))
    :mapping {:y :v}
    :charts [(chart/pp {:x-distribution [:normal] :size 2})]
    :labels {:title "P-P: a t sample against the normal" :y "sample probabilities"}}
   {:width 550 :height 500}))






20.1.3 Kernel densities
One sample, a density per fastmath KDE kernel; chart/function takes the map kernel -> density.
Source: cljplot - kernel densities.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 3)
      data (concat (repeatedly 500 #(r/grandom g 4.5 0.1))
                   (take 10000 (remove #(== (m/round (* (double %) 10.0)) 30.0)
                                       (repeatedly #(+ (r/grandom g 2.0 0.1) (* (r/drandom g) (r/drandom g 1.0 3.0)))))))
      kernels (:kde k/kernel-list)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:charts [(chart/function {:f (mapv (fn [kernel] [(name kernel) (k/kernel-density kernel data)]) kernels)
                              :domain [1.0 6.0] :width 1.5 :mapping {:color :function}})]
    :scales {:color {:title "kernel"}}
    :labels {:title "Kernel densities of one sample"}}
   {:width 800 :height 550}))






20.1.4 Gaussian process
A Gaussian process through ten noisy samples of a sine: the mean, 50 % and 95 % bands, the true function.
Source: cljplot - Gaussian process prediction.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 4)
      truth (fn [x] (+ 10.0 (m/sin (* -0.7 (double x)))))
      xs (repeatedly 10 #(r/drandom g -5 5))
      ys (map #(+ (truth %) (r/grandom g 0.0 0.0005)) xs)
      process (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:normalize? true :kernel (k/kernel :gaussian {:sigma 0.8}) :noise 0.0005})
      xtest (m/slice-range -5.0 5.0 200)
      band (mapv (fn [x [mu sd]] {:x x :mu mu :lo95 (- mu (* 1.96 sd)) :hi95 (+ mu (* 1.96 sd))
                                  :lo50 (- mu (* 0.67 sd)) :hi50 (+ mu (* 0.67 sd))})
                 xtest (gp/predict-all process xtest true))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data band :mapping {:x :x}
    :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo95 :ymax :hi95} :color [130 170 230]})
             (chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo50 :ymax :hi50} :color [70 120 200]})
             (chart/function {:f truth :color [215 48 39] :width 1.5})
             (chart/line {:mapping {:y :mu} :color :black :width 2})
             (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [x y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :mapping {:y :y} :size 9 :color :black})]
    :labels {:title "Gaussian process: mean, 50 % and 95 % bands, the true function (red)" :y nil}}
   {:width 800 :height 500}))




A posterior sample through three points, with its 95 % band (the posterior standard deviation).
Source: cljplot - Gaussian process posterior sample.

(let [xs [-4 1 2] ys [-5 1 2]
      process (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:kernel (k/kernel :gaussian {:sigma 0.8}) :noise 0.005})
      xtest (m/slice-range -5.0 5.0 60)
      rows (mapv (fn [x [y sd]] {:x x :y y :lo (- y (* 1.96 sd)) :hi (+ y (* 1.96 sd))})
                 xtest (gp/posterior-samples process xtest true (r/rng :mersenne 5)))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo :ymax :hi} :color [130 170 230] :interpolator :cubic})
             (chart/line {:color :black :width 2 :interpolator :cubic})
             (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [x y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :size 9 :color :black})]
    :labels {:title "Gaussian process: a posterior sample with its 95 % band"}}
   {:width 800 :height 500}))




Many samples: 30 posterior curves of a periodic kernel through the three points, 20 prior curves of a Gaussian one.
Source: cljplot - Gaussian process posterior and prior samples.

(let [xs [-4 1 2] ys [-5 1 2]
      xtest (m/slice-range -5.0 5.0 40)
      g (r/rng :mersenne 6)
      periodic (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:kernel (k/kernel :periodic {:sigma 0.5 :periodicity 8.0}) :noise 0.0001})
      gaussian (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:kernel (k/kernel :gaussian) :noise 1.0e-7})
      curves (fn [sample-fn n] (vec (for [i (range n) [x y] (map vector xtest (sample-fn))] {:x x :y y :i i})))
      panel (fn [rows title points?]
              {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y :group :i}
               :charts (cond-> [(chart/line {:color [0 0 0 90] :interpolator :cubic})]
                         points? (conj (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [x y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :mapping {:group nil}
                                                       :size 9 :color [215 48 39]})))
               :labels {:title title}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel (curves #(gp/posterior-samples periodic xtest false g) 30) "30 posterior samples (periodic kernel)" true)
                  (panel (curves #(gp/prior-samples gaussian xtest g) 20) "20 prior samples (Gaussian kernel)" false)]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 450}))






20.1.5 Bayesian optimisation
fastmath’s bayesian-optimization maximizes a black box: each step fits a Gaussian process to the points seen so far and evaluates where the expected improvement is highest (dashed rule). Three steps of one run:
Source: cljplot - Bayesian optimisation.

(defn target
  "1D target with two bumps, the higher at x = 2."
  ^double [^double x]
  (+ (m/exp (- (m/sq (- x 2.0)))) (m/exp (- (* 0.1 (m/sq (- x 6.0))))) (/ 1.0 (inc (* x x)))))


(def bo-1d
  (opt/bayesian-optimization target {:bounds [[-2.0 10.0]] :vector-arg? false :init-points 2 :rng (r/rng :mersenne 7)}))


(let [xtest (m/slice-range -2.0 10.0 200)
      step-plot (fn [i]
                  (let [{:keys [xs ys gp util-best]} (nth bo-1d i)
                        band (mapv (fn [x [mu sd]] {:x x :mu mu :lo (- mu (* 1.96 sd)) :hi (+ mu (* 1.96 sd))})
                                   xtest (gp/predict-all gp (map vector xtest) true))]
                    {:data band :mapping {:x :x}
                     :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo :ymax :hi} :color [130 170 230]})
                              (chart/function {:f target :width 2 :color :black})
                              (chart/line {:mapping {:y :mu} :color [30 60 160] :dash [8 3]})
                              (chart/rule {:x (first util-best) :dash [6 4] :width 1.5})
                              (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [[x] y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :mapping {:y :y} :size 8
                                              :color [0 140 140]})]
                     :scales {:y {:domain [-1.0 2.5]}}
                     :labels {:title (str "step " i ", " (count xs) " evaluations") :y nil}}))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange (mapv step-plot [2 6 10]) {:columns 1})
   {:width 800 :height 750}))




A 2D black box: its contours with every evaluated point, the process mean and its standard deviation after 15 steps.
Source: cljplot - Bayesian optimisation.

(defn black-box
  [[x y]]
  (let [x (double x) y (double y)]
    (* (m/sinc (+ 2.0 x y)) (m/sin (+ x x)) (m/cos (+ y y)) (m/sin (* 2.0 x y)))))


(let [bounds {:x [-1.0 0.5] :y [-2.0 -0.5]}
      {:keys [xs gp x]} (nth (opt/bayesian-optimization black-box {:bounds [(:x bounds) (:y bounds)] :vector-arg? true
                                                                   :rng (r/rng :mersenne 8)})
                             15)
      evaluated (map (fn [[a b]] {:x a :y b}) xs)
      panel (fn [title f]
              {:charts [(chart/field {:f f :domain bounds :n 150})
                        (chart/contour {:f f :domain bounds :n 150 :color [255 255 255 120]})
                        (chart/scatter {:data evaluated :mapping {:x :x :y :y} :size 7 :color :black})
                        (chart/scatter {:data [{:x (first x) :y (second x)}] :mapping {:x :x :y :y} :size 14
                                        :shape \x :color [215 48 39]})]
               :scales {:color {:title nil}}
               :aspect :iso
               :labels {:title title}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel "black box and evaluations" black-box)
                  (panel "process mean" (fn [p] (gp/predict gp p)))
                  (panel "process std dev" (fn [p] (second (gp/predict gp p true))))]
                 {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 400}))

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.2 Time series

20.2.1 MA(2)
A moving-average series: each value mixes three consecutive Gaussian shocks.
Source: cljplot - MA(2).

(def ma2
  (let [g (r/rng :mersenne 9)
        e (vec (repeatedly 502 #(r/grandom g)))]
    (mapv (fn [i] (+ (- (double (e (+ i 2)))) (* 0.8 (double (e (inc i)))) (* -0.9 (double (e i))))) (range 500))))


(plot/render-image
 {:data (map-indexed (fn [t y] {:t t :y y}) ma2) :mapping {:x :t :y :y}
  :charts [(chart/line)]
  :labels {:title "MA(2): -e(t) + 0.8 e(t-1) - 0.9 e(t-2)" :x "t" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 280})






20.2.2 Lag plot
Each value against the one seven steps later: an AR(1) series with rare jumps.
Source: cljplot - lag.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 10)
      ar (take 10000 (iterate #(+ (* 0.95 (double %)) (r/grandom g) (if (< (r/drandom g) 0.01) 10.0 0.0)) 0.0))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (series/lag-rows ar 7) :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [0 0 0 30]})]
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "Lag 7 of an AR(1) series with jumps" :x "y(t)" :y "y(t+7)"}}
   {:width 600 :height 600}))






20.2.3 ACF and PACF
The MA(2) series’ autocorrelations cut off after lag 2; its partial autocorrelations decay. Lags outside the band are red.
Source: cljplot - ACF / PACF.

(plot/render-image (plot/acf ma2 {:lags 50 :title "MA(2): ACF and PACF"}) {:width 800 :height 550})

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.3 Functions and fields

(defn fn2d
  [[x y]]
  (let [x (double x) y (double y)]
    (* (- (+ (* x x) (* y y))) (m/sin x) (m/sin y) (m/sin (* x y)))))


(def fn2d-domain {:x [(- m/PI) m/PI] :y [(- m/PI) m/PI]})


20.3.1 A function of two variables
Source: cljplot - function2d.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:f fn2d :domain fn2d-domain :n 300})]
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "-(x^2 + y^2) sin x sin y sin xy"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






20.3.2 Its contours
Source: cljplot - contour2d.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/contour {:f fn2d :domain fn2d-domain :n 300 :fill true :levels 12})]
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "Filled contours of the same function"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






20.3.3 Value noise
Source: cljplot - value noise.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:f (fn [[x y]] (r/vnoise x y)) :domain {:x [-6 6] :y [-6 6]} :n 400})]
  :scales {:color {:range [:black :white]}}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "Value noise"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






20.3.4 A complex function
Domain colouring: the hue is the argument of f(z), the brightness its magnitude wrapped into bands (:log2 - where |f| + 1 doubles), every pixel computed (:pixel-color).
Source: cljplot - complex.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:pixel-color (field/domain-color (fn [z] (cx/div (cx/log z) (cx/sin z))))
                         :domain {:x [-6 6] :y [-6 6]}})]
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "log(z) / sin(z)" :x "re" :y "im"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






20.3.5 Field mapping
Uniform points pushed through a composition of fastmath fields (secant ∘ diamond ∘ power).
Source: cljplot - field.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 11)
      field (f/combine {:type :operation :name :comp
                        :var1 {:type :operation :name :comp
                               :var1 {:type :variation :name :secant :amount 1.0 :config {}}
                               :var2 {:type :variation :name :diamond :amount 1.0 :config {}} :amount 1.0}
                        :var2 {:type :variation :name :power :amount 1.0 :config {}} :amount 1.0})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (vf/mapped-points field (repeatedly 200000 #(vector (r/drandom g -4 4) (r/drandom g -4 4))))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 1 :color [20 40 90 25]})]
    :labels {:title "Points mapped through secant . diamond . power"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))






20.3.6 Vector field
Arrows of the hyperbolic field on a shifted grid, over the sine of its heading.
Source: cljplot - vector field.

(let [hyperbolic (f/field :hyperbolic)
      heading (f/heading hyperbolic)
      domain {:x [-3 3] :y [-3 3]}]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (vf/arrows hyperbolic {:domain domain :n 24 :grid :shifted :scale 1.5})
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :xend :xend :yend :yend}
    :charts [(chart/field {:f (fn [[x y]] (m/sin (heading (v/vec2 x y)))) :domain domain :n 300})
             (chart/segment {:color [90 160 235] :width 1.5 :arrow {:end true :size 5}})]
    :scales {:color {:range [:black :white] :title "sin heading"}
             :x {:domain [-3 3] :expand [0 0]} :y {:domain [-3 3] :expand [0 0]}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "Hyperbolic field"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))






20.3.7 Traces
Points following the exponential field from 3000 random seeds; the traces run off to the right.
Source: cljplot - field trace.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 12)
      seeds (repeatedly 3000 #(vector (r/drandom g -7 7) (r/drandom g -7 7)))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (vf/traces (f/field :exp) seeds {:steps 200 :step 0.01})
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 1 :color [20 70 140 20]})]
    :scales {:x {:domain [-7 7] :nice false} :y {:domain [-7 7] :nice false}}
    :labels {:title "Traces of the exponential field"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.4 Point density

20.4.1 Point cloud
600 000 Gaussian points as a binned density raster.
Source: cljplot - point cloud.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 13)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 600000 (fn [] {:x (r/grandom g) :y (r/grandom g)}))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/field {:binned? true :n 300})]
    :scales {:color {:range [[10 10 40] [60 40 140] [220 90 120] [255 230 160]] :title "density"}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "600 000 points"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))




The same kind of cloud drawn by a chart/image callback: it gets the panel’s scales and size and returns an image - here 200 000 translucent pixels.
Source: cljplot2 - chart/image.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/image {:domain {:x [-4 4] :y [-4 4]}
                         :f (fn [{:keys [x-scale y-scale size]}]
                              (let [[w h] size
                                    g (r/rng :mersenne 14)
                                    canvas (c2d/canvas w h)]
                                (c2d/with-canvas [cv canvas]
                                  (c2d/set-color cv 230 240 255 18)
                                  (dotimes [_ 200000]
                                    (let [x (r/grandom g) y (+ (* 0.6 x) (* 0.8 (r/grandom g)))]
                                      (c2d/rect cv (x-scale x) (y-scale y) 1 1))))
                                canvas))})]
  :theme {:panel {:fill [10 15 40]}}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "A correlated cloud drawn by a callback"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






20.4.2 Hexbin
Two Gaussian clusters counted in flat-topped hexagons.
Source: cljplot - binned heatmap.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 15)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 10000 (fn [] (if (< (r/drandom g) 0.5)
                                     {:x (r/grandom g) :y (r/grandom g)}
                                     {:x (r/grandom g -10 1) :y (r/grandom g -10 1)})))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/bin2d {:cell :flat-hex :bins 30})]
    :scales {:color {:range :prl-9}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "Two clusters in hexagons"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))






20.4.3 Density contours
Old Faithful: the 2D density at a wide and a narrow bandwidth as filled contour bands (nothing below the lowest level), with the eruptions over them.
Source: cljplot - contour. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [faithful (nu/dataset :faithful)
      panel (fn [bandwidth levels title]
              {:data faithful :mapping {:x :waiting :y :eruptions}
               :charts [(chart/contour {:bandwidth bandwidth :levels levels :fill true})
                        (chart/contour {:bandwidth bandwidth :levels levels :color [0 0 0 60]})
                        (chart/scatter {:size 4 :color [20 60 120 200]})]
               :legend false
               :labels {:title title :x "waiting time [min]" :y "eruption time [min]"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel [6.0 0.5] 20 "wide bandwidth, 20 levels") (panel [2.0 0.15] 10 "narrow bandwidth, 10 levels")]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 500}))

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.5 Lines and walks

20.5.1 Reference lines
Horizontal, vertical and sloped rules with dashes and widths, under a sine.
Source: cljplot - lines.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/rule {:y 0 :color :black})
           (chart/rule {:y [1 -1]})
           (chart/rule {:x m/HALF_PI :dash [10 10] :width 5})
           (chart/rule {:x (* 0.75 m/TWO_PI) :dash [10 10] :width 5 :color [128 0 0 100]})
           (chart/rule {:slope (/ 1.0 (* 0.75 m/TWO_PI)) :intercept -1 :dash [1 2 5 2] :width 3})
           (chart/function {:f m/sin :domain [0 m/TWO_PI]})]
  :labels {:title "Rules and a sine"}}
 {:width 900 :height 320})






20.5.2 Wrapped random walk
A drifting 2D walk on a torus: leaving the square on one side, it comes back on the other. A row with a NaN y breaks the line at every wrap; :sort false keeps the walk’s order.
Source: cljplot - wrapped random walk.

(defn- wrap-coordinate
  "`v` wrapped into [-200, 200)."
  ^double [^double v]
  (- (m/mod (+ v 200.0) 400.0) 200.0))


#'galleries.cljplot-extras/wrap-coordinate


(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 16)
      walk (take 3000 (iterate (fn [[x y]] [(+ (double x) 2.0 (r/grandom g 0.0 2.0)) (+ (double y) 0.5 (r/grandom g 0.0 2.0))])
                               [0.0 0.0]))
      wrapped (map (fn [[x y]] [(wrap-coordinate x) (wrap-coordinate y)]) walk)
      rows (mapcat (fn [[[x0 y0] [x1 y1]]]
                     (if (or (> (m/abs (- (double x1) (double x0))) 200.0) (> (m/abs (- (double y1) (double y0))) 200.0))
                       [{:x x0 :y y0} {:x x0 :y ##NaN}]
                       [{:x x0 :y y0}]))
                   (partition 2 1 wrapped))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/line {:sort false :color [0 50 255 150]})]
    :scales {:x {:domain [-200 200]} :y {:domain [-200 200]}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "A random walk on a torus"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.6 Composite

20.6.1 Stacked strips
One sample, many views on a shared x: jittered points, a rug, a box, a histogram and the extent (mean and range) above a violin, a density and a fine histogram below.
Source: cljplot - strips.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 17)
      rows (vec (repeatedly 2000 (fn [] {:v (let [u (r/drandom g)]
                                             (cond (< u 0.5) (r/grandom g)
                                                   (< u 0.65) (r/grandom g -10 2)
                                                   :else (r/grandom g 10 2)))})))
      strip (fn [charts] {:data rows :mapping {:x :v} :charts charts :scales {:x {:domain [-20 20]}} :labels {:x nil :y nil}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(strip [(chart/stripplot {:size 6 :color [215 48 39 30] :rng (r/rng :mersenne 18)})])
                  (strip [(chart/rug)])
                  (strip [(chart/box)])
                  (strip [(chart/histogram {:bins 100 :y :count})])
                  (strip [(chart/extent {:method stats/extent :color :black})])
                  (strip [(chart/violin)])
                  (strip [(chart/density {:fill :color})])
                  (strip [(chart/histogram {:bins 150})])]
                 {:columns 1 :heights [1 1 1 1 1 3 1.5 1.5]})
   {:width 800 :height 800}))






20.6.2 Bubble chart
Seattle’s days: maximal against minimal temperature, coloured by wind, sized (by area) by precipitation.
Source: cljplot - bubble. Data: Seattle daily weather 2012-2015, vega-datasets seattle-weather.csv (NOAA daily observations); licence: vega-datasets is BSD-3-Clause; NOAA data, public domain.

(plot/render-image
 {:data (nu/dataset :seattle-weather)
  :mapping {:x :temp_min :y :temp_max :color :wind :size :precipitation}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:stroke-color :none})]
  :scales {:color {:range (mapv #(c/set-alpha (c/darken (c/color %)) 200) (c/palette :gnbu-9)) :title "wind [m/s]"}
           :size {:range [2 40] :area true :title "precipitation [mm]"}}
  :labels {:title "Seattle weather 2012-2015" :x "minimal temperature [°C]" :y "maximal temperature [°C]"}}
 {:width 750 :height 600})






20.6.3 Heatmap matrices
Random values in a 40 x 40 matrix, and a 15 x 15 one with every cell’s value written in it.
Source: cljplot - heatmap matrix.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 19)
      matrix (fn [n] (vec (for [x (range n) y (range n)] {:x x :y y :value (r/drandom g x (inc y))})))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [{:data (matrix 40) :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :value}
                   :charts [(chart/tile)]
                   :legend false
                   :labels {:title "40 x 40" :x "X" :y "Y"}}
                  {:data (matrix 15) :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :value}
                   :charts [(chart/tile {:value-label (fn [{:keys [value]}] (format "%.1f" (double value)))})]
                   :scales {:color {:range [:yellow :red]}}
                   :legend false
                   :labels {:title "15 x 15, annotated" :x "X" :y "Y"}}]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 520}))






20.6.4 Kernels
Six fastmath kernels as functions of the distance from 0, at full and half scale.
Source: cljplot - kernels (unsaved sketch).

(def kernels [:gaussian :periodic :cauchy :rational-quadratic :matern-12 :matern-52])


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [kernel kernels
                     :let [f (k/kernel kernel)]]
                 {:charts [(chart/function {:f {"full" (fn [x] (f [0.0] [x])) "half" (fn [x] (* 0.5 (double (f [0.0] [x]))))}
                                            :domain [-3 3] :width 2 :mapping {:color :function}})]
                  :scales {:color {:range [[69 117 180] [215 50 40]]}}
                  :legend false
                  :labels {:title (name kernel)}})
               {:columns 3})
 {:width 900 :height 550})






20.6.5 Covariance matrices
The same kernels’ covariance between every pair of points of [-1, 1].
Source: cljplot - covariance matrices (unsaved sketch).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (vec (for [kernel kernels
                   :let [f (k/kernel kernel) points (m/slice-range -1.0 1.0 40)]
                   x points y points]
               {:kernel (name kernel) :x x :y y :value (f [x] [y])}))
  :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :value :facet :kernel}
  :charts [(chart/tile)]
  :scales {:facet {:domain (mapv name kernels)}}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "Covariance matrices" :x nil :y nil}}
 {:width 900 :height 650})






20.6.6 Lollipops
Frequencies of two small samples as lollipops, and a fine histogram as lollipops under its density.
Source: cljplot - frequencies and histogram lollipops (unsaved sketches).

(let [frequencies-rows (fn [sample label offset]
                         (map (fn [[value n]] {:value (+ (double value) (double offset)) :n n :sample label})
                              (frequencies sample)))
      g (r/rng :mersenne 20)
      sample (vec (repeatedly 1300 #(r/grandom g)))
      bins (map (fn [{:keys [mid probability step]}] {:x mid :y (/ (double probability) (double step))})
                (:bins-maps (stats/histogram sample 130)))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [{:data (concat (frequencies-rows [1 2 2 3 1 12 2] "a" -0.12)
                                 (frequencies-rows [3 4 5 4 5 4 3 2 3 4 11 12] "b" 0.12))
                   :mapping {:x :value :y :n :color :sample}
                   :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0}) (chart/scatter {:size 8})]
                   :labels {:title "frequencies" :x "value" :y "count"}}
                  {:data bins :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                   :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0 :color [69 117 180 160]}) (chart/scatter {:size 3})
                            (chart/density {:data (map (fn [v] {:x v}) sample) :mapping {:y nil} :bandwidth 0.04
                                            :fill [215 48 39 80] :color [215 48 39 160]})]
                   :labels {:title "histogram lollipops and a density" :x nil :y "density"}}]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 420}))






20.6.7 Logo
The cljplot2 logo, after the old one: 2500 random pixels of the word, jittered, coloured along x, of random sizes, with density margins. (The same recipe writes img/logo.png in the logo demo - keep the two in sync.)
Source: cljplot - logo.

(let [text-width 250 text-height 85
      logo-font (with-open [in (io/input-stream (io/file "dev/resources/logo/Comfortaa-Bold.ttf"))]
                  (Font/createFont Font/TRUETYPE_FONT in))
      pixels (p/to-pixels (c2d/with-canvas-> (c2d/canvas text-width text-height)
                            (c2d/set-background :black)
                            (c2d/set-color :white)
                            (c2d/set-font (font/resolve-font logo-font :plain 56))
                            (c2d/text "cljplot2" 4 62)))
      g (r/rng :mersenne 2)
      points (->> (repeatedly #(vector (r/irandom g text-width) (r/irandom g text-height)))
                  (filter (fn [[x y]] (pos? (double (c/luma (p/get-color pixels x y))))))
                  (take 2500)
                  (mapv (fn [[x y]] {:x (+ (double x) (r/grandom g))
                                     :y (+ (double (- text-height (long y))) (r/grandom g))
                                     :size (* 10.0 (m/pow (r/drandom g 0.1 1.0) 3.0))})))
      margin-density (chart/density {:fill [60 60 130 170] :color [40 40 100] :mapping {:color nil :size nil}})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data points
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :x :size :size}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:stroke-color :none})]
    :scales {:color {:range (mapv #(c/set-alpha (c/color %) 110) [[30 50 140] [120 50 160] [200 40 90] [230 110 20]])
                     :legend false}
             :size {:range [0.5 10] :area true :legend false}}
    :margins {:top {:charts margin-density :size 22} :right {:charts margin-density :size 22}}
    :labels {:x "cljplot2 - functional plotting library" :y nil}}
   {:width 600 :height 300}))

title: 20  cljplot extras
text:
20.7 Basic charts
The showcase images of the old README, with synthetic data: a skewed sample (skewed, most values 2-8, a tail to 20) and a long-tailed one (tailed, 0 to about 55).

(def skewed
  (let [g (r/rng :mersenne 21)]
    (vec (repeatedly 2000 (fn [] {:v (+ 1.5 (m/exp (r/grandom g 1.0 0.45)))})))))


(def tailed
  (let [d (r/distribution :gamma {:shape 1.2 :scale 8.0 :rng (r/rng :mersenne 22)})]
    (vec (repeatedly 150 (fn [] {:v (r/sample d)})))))


20.7.1 One-dimensional charts
An interval, a box with points, a density line, extents (minimum - mean - maximum), a rug and strips of points.
Source: cljplot showcase - bar, box, density-line, min-max-mean, rug, strip, strip-distorted (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7).

(let [strip (fn [title data charts] {:data data :mapping {:x :v} :charts charts :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})
      halves [{:v -20.0} {:v 10.0}]]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(strip "interval" halves [(chart/extent {:method :min-max :center :none :line-width 22})])
                  (strip "box with points" tailed [(chart/box {:outliers true}) (chart/stripplot {:size 6 :rng (r/rng :mersenne 23)})])
                  (strip "density" skewed [(chart/density)])
                  (strip "min - mean - max" tailed [(chart/extent {:method stats/extent :shape \V :size 12})
                                                    (chart/rug {:color [69 117 180 160]})])
                  (strip "rug" tailed [(chart/rug {:thickness 16})])
                  (strip "distorted strip" tailed [(chart/stripplot {:size 9 :color [69 117 180 60] :rng (r/rng :mersenne 24)})])
                  (strip "strip" tailed [(chart/stripplot {:size 9 :jitter 0.0 :color [69 117 180 90]})])]
                 {:columns 1})
   {:width 800 :height 800}))






20.7.2 Distributions
A filled density, a violin with its box, a mirrored histogram of two samples and a histogram in percent.
Source: cljplot showcase - density, violin, histogram, histogram-percents (1, 2, 3, 4).

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 25)
      two (vec (concat (map #(assoc % :sample "a") skewed)
                       (repeatedly 2000 (fn [] {:v (+ 1.5 (m/exp (r/grandom g 1.1 0.35))) :sample "b"}))))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [{:data skewed :mapping {:x :v} :charts [(chart/density {:fill :color})] :labels {:title "density" :x nil}}
                  {:data skewed :mapping {:x :v} :charts [(chart/violin {:inner :box})] :labels {:title "violin" :x nil :y nil}}
                  {:data two :mapping {:x :v :color :sample} :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 60})]
                   :labels {:title "mirrored histogram" :x nil}}
                  {:data skewed :mapping {:x :v} :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 60 :y :percent})]
                   :labels {:title "histogram, percent" :x nil}}]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 600}))






20.7.3 Lollipop histogram
Bin counts as lollipops, the sample as a strip on top.
Source: cljplot showcase - lollipops2.

(plot/render-image
 {:data (map (fn [{:keys [mid count]}] {:x mid :y count}) (:bins-maps (stats/histogram (map :v skewed) 60)))
  :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
  :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0}) (chart/scatter {:size 5})]
  :margins {:top {:charts (chart/stripplot {:data skewed :mapping {:x :v} :size 5 :color [69 117 180 60]
                                            :rng (r/rng :mersenne 26)})
                  :size 30}}
  :labels {:title "Lollipop histogram" :x nil :y "count"}}
 {:width 900 :height 550})






20.7.4 Bars
Two groups per category, side by side, negative values to the left.
Source: cljplot showcase - bars.

(plot/render-image
 {:data [{:c "a" :g "1" :v -21} {:c "a" :g "2" :v -3.8} {:c "b" :g "1" :v -2.1} {:c "b" :g "2" :v 18}
         {:c "c" :g "1" :v 33} {:c "c" :g "2" :v 22} {:c "d" :g "1" :v 11} {:c "d" :g "2" :v 22}]
  :mapping {:x :v :y :c :color :g}
  :charts [(chart/bar {:position :dodge})]
  :labels {:title "Dodged bars" :x nil :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 550})






20.7.5 Connected scatter
Twenty points joined in their order by a smooth parametric curve, sized by a value.
Source: cljplot showcase - connected.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 27)
      rows (vec (repeatedly 20 (fn [] {:x (r/drandom g 6 17) :y (r/drandom g 0 8) :s (r/drandom g)})))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/line {:sort false :curve :parametric :color [69 117 180]})
             (chart/scatter {:mapping {:size :s} :color [150 30 30]})]
    :scales {:size {:range [4 22] :legend false}}
    :labels {:title "Connected scatter"}}
   {:width 800 :height 600}))






20.7.6 Dense scatter
5000 points of two bounded, correlated variables with quantised values (the original’s data, Kaggle columns cont4 / cont8, aren’t available): bands show the quantisation.
Source: cljplot showcase - cont4_cont8.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 28)
      quantise (fn [v steps] (/ (m/round (* (double v) steps)) steps))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 5000 (fn [] (let [u (r/drandom g)
                                        x (m/constrain (+ 0.2 (* 0.75 u) (r/grandom g 0.0 0.12)) 0.18 0.97)
                                        y (m/constrain (+ 0.25 (* 0.6 u) (r/grandom g 0.0 0.15)) 0.25 0.98)]
                                    {:x (quantise x 150) :y (quantise y 90)})))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 5 :color [40 80 160 120]})]
    :labels {:title "Two quantised variables" :x "cont4" :y "cont8"}}
   {:width 600 :height 600}))






20.7.7 Noise curves
Three curves of value noise.
Source: cljplot showcase - functions.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/function {:f {"a" (fn [x] (r/vnoise (* 3.0 (double x)) 0.5))
                                "b" (fn [x] (r/vnoise (* 3.0 (double x)) 10.5))
                                "c" (fn [x] (r/vnoise (* 3.0 (double x)) 20.5))}
                            :domain [-4 4] :mapping {:color :function}})]
  :labels {:title "Value noise curves"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 320})






20.7.8 Line with a spline
A random series, its points and a cubic spline through them.
Source: cljplot showcase - line.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 29)
      rows (map-indexed (fn [i y] {:x i :y y}) (reductions + 10.0 (repeatedly 99 #(r/grandom g 0 1.5))))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator :cubic :color [200 40 120] :width 1.5})
             (chart/line {:color [69 117 180 150]})
             (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
    :labels {:title "A line, its points and a spline"}}
   {:width 800 :height 600}))






20.7.9 Rugs per category
Source: cljplot showcase - rugs.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 30)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (concat (repeatedly 1000 (fn [] {:c "a" :v (r/grandom g -0.2 0.9)}))
                  (repeatedly 1000 (fn [] {:c "b" :v (r/grandom g 2.0 1.2)})))
    :mapping {:x :c :y :v}
    :charts [(chart/rug {:color [69 117 180 60]})]
    :labels {:title "A rug per category" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 450 :height 450}))






20.7.10 Scatter with histograms
Source: cljplot showcase - scatter-sides.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 31)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 1000 (fn [] (let [x (r/drandom g -7 18)] {:x x :y (+ (* 1.4 x) 5.0 (r/grandom g 0 4))})))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3})]
    :margins {:top {:charts (chart/histogram {:bins 15})} :right {:charts (chart/histogram {:bins 20})}}
    :labels {:title "Scatter with histogram margins"}}
   {:width 600 :height 600}))






20.7.11 Two groups with a rug
Source: cljplot showcase - scatters2-rug.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 32)
      group (fn [n mu sd label] (repeatedly n (fn [] {:x (r/grandom g mu sd) :y (r/grandom g mu sd)
                                                      :s (m/pow (r/drandom g) 4.0) :g label})))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (concat (group 1000 0.0 1.0 "a") (group 100 2.0 0.8 "b"))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :color :g :size :s}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:stroke-color :none})]
    :margins {:right {:charts (chart/rug {:mapping {:size nil} :thickness 16}) :size 25}}
    :scales {:color {:range [[60 100 220 200] [140 20 20 120]]} :size {:range [2 18] :legend false}}
    :labels {:title "Two groups, sized points, a rug of y"}}
   {:width 800 :height 600}))

title: 21  Lattice
text:
21.1 Chapter 1 - Introduction
The figures of Deepayan Sarkar’s Lattice: Multivariate Data Visualization with R (Springer 2008), rebuilt with cljplot2 - a section per chapter, a block per figure. The R code of every figure is on the book’s figures page; each block links its figure there.
The figures show the same information as the originals; styling differs, and the code is cljplot2’s own (plain plot maps, data prepared in Clojure). Lattice’s banking (aspect = "xy") is replaced by the image size, its strips by cljplot2 facet strips. Lattice fills panels from the bottom row up; here they run top-down, so panels stacked in rows and ordered by a statistic put the largest first to look the same. 3D boxes are drawn in perspective at lattice’s distance of 0.2 (:view {:distance 0.2}; cljplot2’s default is orthographic), from lattice’s views: screen = list(z = θ, x = φ) is :view {:azimuth -θ :elevation (90 + φ)} (the default z = 40, x = -60 - azimuth -40, elevation 30). Data are the book’s, exported from R (see the dataset notes under each figure).
Not here: chapter 12 (interactive displays) and a few figures outside the medium - each is listed in its chapter.

title: 21  Lattice
21  Lattice
section: 21.2 Chapter 2 - A Technical Overview of lattice

title: 21  Lattice
text:
21.3 Chapter 3 - Visualizing Univariate Distributions

21.3.1 Fig 3.1 Kernel density
Old Faithful eruption times: a Gaussian kernel density, the values as jittered points along the bottom edge.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.1. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful
  :mapping {:x :eruptions}
  :charts [(chart/density) (chart/stripplot {:place :edge :thickness 16 :rng (r/rng :mersenne 31)})]
  :labels {:x "eruptions" :y "Density"}}
 {:width 600 :height 450})






21.3.2 Fig 3.2 Rectangular kernel
A rectangular kernel of standard deviation 0.2 (R’s bw) - half-width 0.2 √3 - at 200 points.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.2. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful
  :mapping {:x :eruptions}
  :charts [(chart/density {:kernel :uniform :bandwidth (* 0.2 (m/sqrt 3.0)) :n 200}) (chart/rug {:thickness 16})]
  :labels {:x "eruptions" :y "Density"}}
 {:width 600 :height 450})






21.3.3 Fig 3.3 Densities by day
Flow cytometry of a graft-versus-host-disease patient: log forward scatter, a panel per day after transplant.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.3. Data: Flow cytometry of a GvHD patient, 10 days, R latticeExtra package gvhd10 (Brinkman et al. 2007); licence: GPL (>= 2) (latticeExtra).

(def gvhd10-log
  "gvhd10 with log and log2 forward scatter."
  (mapv (fn [{:keys [fsc-h] :as row}] (assoc row :log-fsc (m/log fsc-h) :log2-fsc (m/log2 fsc-h))) gvhd10))


(plot/render-image
 {:data gvhd10-log
  :mapping {:x :log-fsc :facet :days}
  :charts [(chart/density)]
  :facets {:columns 2}
  :labels {:x "log(FSC.H)" :y "Density"}}
 {:width 700 :height 750})






21.3.4 Fig 3.4 Histograms on the density scale
Source: Lattice Fig 3.4. Data: Flow cytometry of a GvHD patient, 10 days, R latticeExtra package gvhd10 (Brinkman et al. 2007); licence: GPL (>= 2) (latticeExtra).

(plot/render-image
 {:data gvhd10-log
  :mapping {:x :log2-fsc :facet :days}
  :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 50 :y :density})]
  :facets {:columns 2}
  :labels {:x "log Forward Scatter" :y "Density"}}
 {:width 700 :height 750})






21.3.5 Fig 3.5 Normal Q-Q plots
GCSE score quantiles against the standard normal, a panel per A-level score.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.5. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:y :gcsescore :facet :score}
  :charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal] :size 2 :line false})]
  :facets {:columns 3}
  :labels {:x "qnorm" :y "gcsescore"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






21.3.6 Fig 3.6 Grouped Q-Q plots
Source: Lattice Fig 3.6. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:y :gcsescore :color :score :facet :gender}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal] :size 3 :line false})]
  :facets {:columns 2}
  :labels {:x "Standard Normal Quantiles" :y "Average GCSE Score"}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






21.3.7 Fig 3.7 A power transformation
GCSE score to the power 2.34 makes the score groups’ quantile curves nearly straight and parallel.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.7. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(def chem97-trans
  "chem97 with the transformed GCSE score `gcsescore^2.34`."
  (mapv #(assoc % :gcsescore-trans (m/pow (:gcsescore %) 2.34)) chem97))


(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97-trans
  :mapping {:y :gcsescore-trans :color :score :facet :gender}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical :title "score"}}
  :charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal] :size 3 :line false})]
  :facets {:columns 2}
  :labels {:x "Standard Normal Quantiles" :y "Transformed GCSE Score"}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






21.3.8 Fig 3.8 Empirical CDFs
Source: Lattice Fig 3.8. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(def chem97-positive (filterv #(pos? (:gcsescore %)) chem97))


(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97-positive
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :color :gender :facet :score}
  :charts [(chart/ecdf)]
  :facets {:columns 3}
  :labels {:x "Average GCSE Score" :y "Empirical CDF"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






21.3.9 Fig 3.9 Uniform Q-Q plots
Quantiles against the uniform distribution: the empirical CDF with the axes swapped.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.9. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97-positive
  :mapping {:y :gcsescore :color :gender :facet :score}
  :charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:uniform-real] :size 3 :line false})]
  :facets {:columns 6}
  :labels {:x "Uniform quantiles" :y "Average GCSE Score"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






21.3.10 Fig 3.10 Two-sample Q-Q plots
100 quantiles of the boys’ scores against the girls’, per A-level score (ppoints(100) probabilities), and the line y = x.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.10. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(let [ps (mapv #(/ (- % 0.5) 100.0) (range 1 101))
      quantiles (fn [rows] (stats/quantiles (map :gcsescore rows) ps))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (for [[score rows] (group-by :score chem97)
                :let [by-gender (group-by :gender rows)]
                [f m] (map vector (quantiles (by-gender "F")) (quantiles (by-gender "M")))]
            {:score score :f f :m m})
    :mapping {:x :m :y :f :facet :score}
    :charts [(chart/scatter) (chart/rule {:slope 1 :intercept 0 :color :grey})]
    :facets {:columns 3}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:x "M" :y "F"}}
   {:width 800 :height 600}))






21.3.11 Fig 3.11 Box plots
Source: Lattice Fig 3.11. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :y (levels/categorical :score) :facet :gender}
  :scales {:facet {:domain ["M" "F"]}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :facets {:columns 2}
  :labels {:x "Average GCSE Score" :y "score"}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






21.3.12 Fig 3.12 Box widths by group size
Source: Lattice Fig 3.12. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97-trans
  :mapping {:x :gender :y :gcsescore-trans :facet :score}
  :scales {:x {:domain ["M" "F"]}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:varwidth true})]
  :facets {:columns 6}
  :labels {:x nil :y "Transformed GCSE score"}}
 {:width 900 :height 400})

Source: Lattice Fig 3.13. Data: Flow cytometry of a GvHD patient, 10 days, R latticeExtra package gvhd10 (Brinkman et al. 2007); licence: GPL (>= 2) (latticeExtra).

  :mapping {:x :log-fsc :y (levels/categorical :days)}

Tails 3 bandwidths past the data (:cut 3, R’s density default as lattice uses it).

21.3.15 Fig 3.15 Strip plot
Earthquake depth by magnitude, one strip per magnitude value.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.15. Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data quakes
  :mapping {:x :depth :y (levels/categorical :mag)}
  :charts [(chart/stripplot {:jitter 0})]
  :labels {:x "depth" :y "mag"}}
 {:width 600 :height 700})






21.3.16 Fig 3.16 Jittered strips
Source: Lattice Fig 3.16. Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data quakes
  :mapping {:x (levels/categorical :mag) :y :depth}
  :charts [(chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 316)})]
  :labels {:x "Magnitude (Richter)" :y "Depth (km)"}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






21.3.17 Fig 3.17 Residuals and their medians
Square roots of the absolute residuals of an additive model of barley yield (variety + year + site, least squares on dummy-coded factors), jittered by site (in R’s order), a line through each year’s medians; two contrasting colours for the years.
Source: Lattice Fig 3.17. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(def barley-residuals
  "barley with `:root-residual` - the square root of the absolute residual of the additive least-squares model of
  yield on variety, year and site (dummy-coded factors)."
  (let [dummies (vec (for [k [:variety :year :site], level (rest (sort (distinct (map k barley))))] [k level]))
        model (regression/lm (mapv :yield barley)
                             (mapv (fn [row] (mapv (fn [[k level]] (if (= level (k row)) 1.0 0.0)) dummies)) barley))]
    (mapv (fn [row residual] (assoc row :root-residual (m/sqrt (m/abs residual))))
          barley (get-in model [:residuals :raw]))))


(def barley-residual-plot
  "The residuals jittered by site (R's order), a line through each year's medians (in site order, left to right)."
  (let [by-site-year (group-by (juxt :site :year) barley-residuals)
        sites (nu/levels :barley :site)
        medians (for [site sites year [1931 1932]]
                  {:site site :year year :median (stats/median (map :root-residual (by-site-year [site year])))})]
    {:data barley-residuals
     :mapping {:x :site :y :root-residual :color :year}
     :scales {:x {:domain sites} :color {:type :categorical :range two-colors}}
     :charts [(chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 317)})
              (chart/line {:data medians :mapping {:y :median}})]
     :labels {:x nil :y "√|Residual Barley Yield|"}}))


(plot/render-image barley-residual-plot {:width 800 :height 450})

21.5 Chapter 5 - Scatter Plots and Extensions

Source: Lattice Fig 5.2. Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

21.5.3 Fig 5.3 Depth as groups
Depth cut at its terciles: three groups of equal size, coloured.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.3. Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (levels/bin quakes :depth {:as :depth-cut :bins {:quantiles 3}})
  :mapping {:x :long :y :lat :color :depth-cut}
  :scales {:color {:title "Depth"}}

(def quakes-by-depth
  "quakes, deepest first."
  (vec (sort-by :depth > quakes)))


(def grey-depth
  "Colour scale of depth: grey levels as R's `gray.colors`, dark for shallow."

(plot/render-image
 {:data quakes-by-depth
  :mapping {:x :long :y :lat :color :depth}
  :scales grey-depth

A panel per magnitude interval: a shingle of four equal-count, half-overlapping intervals.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.5. Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

  :mapping {:x :long :y :lat :color :depth :facet :magnitude}

Source: Lattice Fig 5.6. Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

  :facets {:columns 2}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:x "Longitude" :y "Latitude"}}
 {:width 750 :height 800})






21.5.7 Fig 5.7 Plot types
Lattice’s type argument drawn with cljplot2 charts on one seeded data set: points, lines in data order, both, a regression line, the grid alone, steps (two kinds), stems, averages per x, a loess curve. The bottom row repeats the last five with x and y exchanged (lattice’s horizontal = TRUE): the same charts of the swapped columns in a :flip plot.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.7.

(let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 2007041)
      grid-xs (mapv #(+ -10.0 (* 20.0 (/ % 14.0))) (range 15))
      xy (vec (for [_ (range 30)
                    :let [x (grid-xs (r/irandom rng 15))]]
                {:x x :y (+ x (* 0.25 (m/sq (+ x 1.0))) (r/grandom rng 0.0 5.0))}))
      sorted (sort-by :x xy)
      steps (fn [corner] (concat (mapcat (fn [a b] [a (corner a b)]) sorted (rest sorted)) [(last sorted)]))
      averages (for [[x rs] (sort-by key (group-by :x xy))] {:x x :y (stats/mean (map :y rs))})
      types [["p" xy [(chart/scatter)]]
             ["l" xy [(chart/line {:sort false})]]
             ["o" xy [(chart/line {:sort false}) (chart/scatter)]]
             ["r" xy [(chart/smooth {:method :lm :band :none})]]
             ["g" xy [(chart/scatter {:color [0 0 0 0]})]]
             ["s" (steps (fn [a b] {:x (:x b) :y (:y a)})) [(chart/line {:sort false})]]
             ["S" (steps (fn [a b] {:x (:x a) :y (:y b)})) [(chart/line {:sort false})]]
             ["h" xy [(chart/segment {:yend 0})]]
             ["a" averages [(chart/line)]]
             ["smooth" xy [(chart/smooth {:band :none})]]]
      panel (fn [[title data charts]]
              {:data data :mapping {:x :x :y :y} :charts charts
               :labels {:title (str "\"" title "\"") :x nil :y nil}})
      swapped (mapv (fn [{:keys [x y]}] {:x y :y x}) xy)]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange (concat (map panel types)
                         ;; horizontal: the same charts of the swapped columns, drawn flipped
                         (for [[title _ charts] (drop 5 types)
                               :let [sorted (sort-by :x swapped)
                                     data (case title
                                            "s" (concat (mapcat (fn [a b] [a {:x (:x b) :y (:y a)}]) sorted (rest sorted)) [(last sorted)])
                                            "S" (concat (mapcat (fn [a b] [a {:x (:x a) :y (:y b)}]) sorted (rest sorted)) [(last sorted)])
                                            "a" (for [[x rs] (sort-by key (group-by :x swapped))] {:x x :y (stats/mean (map :y rs))})
                                            swapped)]]
                           (assoc (panel [(str title ", horizontal") data charts]) :flip true)))
                 {:columns 5})
   {:width 1000 :height 650}))






21.5.8 Fig 5.8 Scatter plot with a loess curve
Peak ground acceleration against distance from the epicentre, for 23 Californian earthquakes.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.8. Data: Western US earthquakes: ground acceleration, R MEMSS package Earthquake (Joyner & Boore 1981); licence: GPL (>= 2) (MEMSS).

(def earthquake-labels {:x "Distance From Epicenter (km)" :y "Maximum Horizontal Acceleration (g)"})

  :mapping {:x :distance :y :accel}
  :charts [(chart/scatter) (chart/smooth {:band :none})]
  :labels earthquake-labels}
 {:width 650 :height 500})






21.5.9 Fig 5.9 Logarithmic axes
Source: Lattice Fig 5.9. Data: Western US earthquakes: ground acceleration, R MEMSS package Earthquake (Joyner & Boore 1981); licence: GPL (>= 2) (MEMSS).

(def log2-axes
  "Base-2 logarithmic x and y scales labelled as powers of two."
  {:x {:kind :log :base 2 :formatter :power} :y {:kind :log :base 2 :formatter :power}})


(plot/render-image
 {:data earthquake
  :mapping {:x :distance :y :accel}
  :scales log2-axes
  :charts [(chart/scatter) (chart/smooth {:band :none})]
  :labels earthquake-labels}
 {:width 650 :height 500})






21.5.10 Fig 5.10 Local fits by magnitude
A panel per magnitude interval (three equal-count intervals overlapping by 10 %): a loess curve per panel (the book uses locfit) and the least-squares line of all quakes on the log-log scale, the same in every panel.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.10. Data: Western US earthquakes: ground acceleration, R MEMSS package Earthquake (Joyner & Boore 1981); licence: GPL (>= 2) (MEMSS).

(let [model (regression/lm (mapv #(m/log2 (:accel %)) earthquake) (mapv (fn [row] [(m/log2 (:distance row))]) earthquake))
      intercept (:intercept model)
      slope (first (:beta model))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (shingle/shingle earthquake :richter {:count 3 :overlap 0.1 :as :magnitude :label "Magnitude"})
    :mapping {:x :distance :y :accel :facet :magnitude}
    :scales log2-axes
    :charts [(chart/scatter)
             (chart/smooth {:band :none :color :grey :width 2})
             (chart/function {:f (fn [d] (m/pow 2.0 (+ intercept (* slope (m/log2 d))))) :color :black})]
    :facets {:columns 3}
    :labels earthquake-labels}
   {:width 900 :height 400}))






21.5.11 Fig 5.11 Several variables against one
Seattle-Tacoma weather, January to March 2007: minimum and maximum temperature and rainfall by day.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.11. Data: Seattle-Tacoma airport weather, Jan-Mar 2007, R latticeExtra package SeatacWeather (NOAA); licence: GPL (>= 2) (latticeExtra).

Rainfall scaled to the temperature range (× 80 / its maximum) and drawn as stems.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.12. Data: Seattle-Tacoma airport weather, Jan-Mar 2007, R latticeExtra package SeatacWeather (NOAA); licence: GPL (>= 2) (latticeExtra).

(def max-precip (reduce max (keep :precip seatac)))


(plot/render-image
 {:data seatac
  :mapping {:x :day :facet :month}
  :scales months
  :charts [(chart/line {:mapping {:y :min-temp} :color :black})
           (chart/line {:mapping {:y :max-temp} :color :black})
           (chart/segment {:data (map #(update % :precip (fn [p] (some-> p (* 80.0) (/ max-precip)))) seatac)
                           :mapping {:y :precip} :yend 0 :color :black})]
  :facets {:columns 3}
  :labels {:x "day" :y "Temperature and Rainfall"}}
 {:width 900 :height 400})






21.5.13 Fig 5.13 Temperature and rainfall, each on its own axis
The book adds a rainfall axis on the right of one panel; cljplot2 has no secondary axes, so the two measures are two plots - each with its own axis.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.13. Data: Seattle-Tacoma airport weather, Jan-Mar 2007, R latticeExtra package SeatacWeather (NOAA); licence: GPL (>= 2) (latticeExtra).

(plot/render-image

                 :mapping {:x :day :y :value :group :variable :facet :month}
                 :scales months
                 :charts [(chart/line {:color :black})]
                 :facets {:columns 3}
                 :labels {:x nil :y "Temperature (Fahrenheit)"}}
                {:data seatac
                 :mapping {:x :day :y :precip :facet :month}
                 :scales months
                 :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0 :color :black})]
                 :facets {:columns 3}
                 :labels {:x "day" :y "Rainfall (inches)"}}]
               {:columns 1})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






21.5.14 Fig 5.14 Hexagonal binning
Two fluorescence channels of the GvHD cells (asinh-transformed), counted in hexagons, a panel per day; grey levels by the square root of the count (:transform :sqrt, lattice’s trans = sqrt).
Source: Lattice Fig 5.14. Data: Flow cytometry of a GvHD patient, 10 days, R latticeExtra package gvhd10 (Brinkman et al. 2007); licence: GPL (>= 2) (latticeExtra).

  :mapping {:x :fl2 :y :ssc :facet :days}

  :labels {:x "asinh(FL2.H)" :y "asinh(SSC.H)"}}
 {:width 900 :height 550})






21.5.15 Fig 5.15 Scatter-plot matrix
Source: Lattice Fig 5.15. Data: Violent crime rates by US state (1973), R datasets package USArrests (McNeil 1977); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

Arrest rates of the states of each census region (joined from the state facts): points and a loess curve with lattice’s panel.loess settings (span 2/3, degree 1) - with a dozen states per region, ggplot2’s degree 2 bends.
Source: Lattice Fig 5.16. Data: Violent crime rates by US state (1973), R datasets package USArrests (McNeil 1977); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [region (into {} (map (juxt :name :region) states))
      rows (map #(assoc % :region (region (:state %))) us-arrests)

                   (plot/pairs (filterv #(= r (:region %)) rows)

                              :drat "Axle ratio" :wt "Weight" :qsec "1/4 mile time"}})
